	Drifters who ascend to become Leaders often forsake their nature not soon after, their

	If the Drifter is an Exo or a Mutant, they will be relying on the Species Creation System to

Å@Å@Å@The Exo and Mutant Deviation is how far away from the ÅgHuman StandardÅh the Exo or Mutant 
actually is. With ExoÅfs coming from all walks of life, a few are inevitably going to look human enough to 
blend in to society, while some Mutants are little more than a freakish collection of limbs stapled 
together that claims to be human.
Å@Å@Å@This Deviation Principle also grants both Exos and Mutants a number of Expressions - 
Expressions are non-mechanical aspects that further differentiate the Drifter from the human 
average. Expressions represent the little changes, such as unique hair colors or odd skin complexion. 
These may also represent quirky abilities that donÅft do much of use, but may indicate flavorful or useful 
aspects that the Drifter needs to survive in the world - such as Vestigial Wings, Complex Feeding 
Apparatus, or growing fruit from their plantoid body.

Robotica Cyberntica
	If the Drifter is a Robot or indulging in cybernetics, they will need to consult the Robotics 
Creation System to determine their new make, creation, and additional effects that come from being 
synthetic. Similar to Species Rating, the Robot will need to determine their Robotics Chassis Rating to 
determine how much is packed into their system. The more they have, the more difficult it is for them 
to Transfer out of their steel exterior and actually develop themselves successfully.

	When a Robot is being designed they have their Base Attribute Choices already established, 
rather than relying on the whims of fate to actually do such. These are mostly designed around which 
kind of parts are being used to build them and the skill of the craftsmen who brought them to life. 
	They will also need to worry about their Human Deviation Index similarly to the Exos, but rather 
than being outright horror or revulsion, the Robot must contend with being too alien to be fitted or 
repaired correctly without the right parts. A specialized Robot built for purpose with parts only found 
in one factory may be difficult to repair and save them when it goes all wrong.

Cybertroniks
	Drifters who lose limbs willingly or not will most likely begin indulging in Cybernetics to 
compensate for the lack of other aspects. They will first need to calculate to see how much their body 
can sustain through the use of their Cybernetic Stress. 

Cybernetic Stress Calculation
[HRD]
If Cybernetic Stress Exceeds Limit, reduce HP to compensate.

	Basic Cybernetics allow the Drifter to augment various aspects of their body by replacing limbs 
or other essential components with technology. Base Cybernetics (Cyber Arm, Cyber Legs, etc) are 
entirely defined by their Modifier which the Drifter will need to determine and purchase when they 
find what they like. For example, a Cybertronik Arm that is Standard Grade granting a +2 to POW 
would be 2000 Credits with the amount of Cybernetic Stress is takes being (2 * 1d10). Every installation 
runs the risk of exceeding their Cybernetic Stress as their body begins to fail rapidly on the operating 
table.

Within the Bermuda Triangle, rumors of the sunken island 
of Atlantis exist, and different occultist groups want to rise 
the island again to recover the sorcerous secrets and 
technology that exist in Atlantis. - Sex Pistols

What was once Haiti has become a land where voodoo 
priests call spirits, create zombies, mind controlled undead 
servants, and control different territories alongside gangs 
who fight for power among themselves. - Sex Pistols

The Free Republic of Yanks: Also called the "Kingdom of 
New Hampshire" or "New New England", this is a territory 
which makes up the entirety of New Hampshire's historical 
borders alongside some of western Maine, eastern 
Vermont, and northern western Massachusetts. This 
"nation" is a semi-recent creation formed from those who 
read about the birth of the United States, some bits and 
pieces of New England's history, and a whole lot of legend 
and mythologizing of historical figures. - Cole

These people revere the likes of George Washington and 
Thomas Jefferson, calling on them like holy patrons and 
citing their (dubiously sourced) writings where they 
predicted the Exos coming to Earth, and wish to spread 
their "religion" far and wide. The nation is equally strange; 
with both a Monarch and a President. Both share power 
semi-equally, though it's not a Constitutional Monarchy. It's 
more...the king is the president, the president is the vice 
president. It's confusing. THEY are very confused. - Cole

Memetic Virus An area of the galaxy has been put under 
lockdown after rumors of a being whose name I cannot 
divulge having his boots stolen were spread out. Although 
seemingly inoffensive, it has the eerie side effect of being 
transmitted for no reason and in full, losing not a single 
detail in a chain thousands of members long. It has been 
diagnosed that beings exposed to this rumor have an itch 
to share it with everyone they find, and yet will never 
attempt to with someone that already knows it, even if 
those two individuals had never met before. - Dodoianon

A merchant that will sell you what you need, in your 
greatest time of desperation. Nothing more and nothing 
less, he doesn't barter in monetary currency. but with 
favors, your time, and effort. They have saved many towns 
and villages. For those who know what they're dealing 
with, happily pay the price. But no one really knows if they 
are something of a higher power or a lower power. All they 
know is that they are something greater that tries to 
assume the guys of a humble merchant. - Solidcrazyy 


Stragglers from Beyond: A group of Exos and even 
Humans come from one singular place sometimes, and 
recognize one another as members from that old world. 
They often speak of coming from "Morta IV", a galaxy 
which they're aware they're no longer in considering this 
one is called "The Milky Way", a name nobody used for 
their old galaxy. Typically, these wayward individuals went 
through a Dimensional Gate on their side, intending to 
travel to another destination...and somehow, their 
destination was screwed up in the process?landing them 
here. 
Many of these Exos are weirded out by the coexistence of 
magic and technology, as where they come from one 
actively restricts the other and vice versa...however, they 
are willing to adapt if given the chance. Often Exos from 
"Morta IV" actually put out jobs asking people to find 
information about Earth, as they wish to learn the history of 
Earth if at all possible, deciding if this is to be their new 
home they should at least get acquainted with. - Cole

WARNING!
	The fictional world of Errant Earth (?) is quite violent and deadly. It is an exotic realm where 
magic is as real as technology and demonic creatures plague humankind. 
	Some parents may find the violence and supernatural elements of the game inappropriate for 
young readers or players. We suggest parental discretion. 
	None of us at The SPRUG Workshop (?) condone , nor encourage, the Occult, the Practice of 
Magic, the use of drugs, or violence. 
 
	ThereÅfs something magical about that opening text crawl for me. Palladium Games, my dearly 
beloved Uncle Kev and company created one of the most fascinating settings IÅfve ever had the love of 
running and playing in. My story with RIFTS begins back when I first started playing TTRPGs in general, 
my affection for Warhammer Fantasy 2e, being recruited into a homebrewed Castles & Crusades 
campaign - twice, and even opening that book for the first time with Mike and Terry. I think I would be 
remiss if I didnÅft mention all of that original group of RIFTS players. The dozens of books, the hours of 
playing in that basement, and the calming walks home after it.
	ItÅfs nostalgic to me, a strange place for a strange time in my life. I think I was lucky, really lucky, 
for the people I knew and the time I had with them. Perhaps thatÅfs why RIFTS holds a special place in 
my heart. An appreciation for a time long gone. Though not to say I havenÅft stopped my love for 
RIFTS, I reference it frequently, terms have been lifted, and RIFTS 2 was always there as a funny 
stretch goal.
	I remember writing down RIFTS 2 when I adopted the name Notepad Anon. Years ago now. It 
was always in the back of my mind, each game a refinement to reach my ultimate goal of RIFTS 2. 
D20/100 was made for a game that I havenÅft thought about in a long while, it was refined by one 
obsession project to capture the heart, and further twisted and refined to get what I wanted. Metal 
Saviors? Please, that was just one step in this obsession. Though I think that leads into why I fear to 
work on RIFTS 2, now Errant Earth.
	Is this the refinement of it all? The last huzzah? Most likely this will be my last game before I 
take a job in a foreign country. So Errant Earth is perhaps a large-scale autobiography about 
nostalgia, inevitability, and look into the mind of a TTRPG Developer. I also get to add gratuitous 
writing masturbation for me - there will be nothing elegant about the lore of Errant Earth, it will be my 
mind on full display, its rules will be my hands, and its breath will be my life.
	If RIFTS is Uncle KevÅfs great hurrah, then perhaps Errant Earth will be the grand hurrah for the 
SPRUG Workshop. God help us all.

Temptation
Å@Å@Å@The Old World was lost in fire and brimstone. To most, that description is enough; to many 
more, they donÅft know more than that. The exact year, according to the calendars of the Old World, is 
2688?four hundred years since anything relevant could be recorded outside the few panicked death 
oaths by renegade soldiers, the explanations of why the Old World fell by new messiahs and would-be 
tyrants, and the occasional metal album from bands long dead.
Å@Å@Å@The final years of the Old World are marked by an apocalyptic tale?something that haunts 
every story told from the old logs. Nuclear annihilation caused a chain reaction that destroyed 
everything. One day they are, and the next, they are not. Piecing together the dark ages that followed 
is difficult; the savage heart of man met the death throes of the shining civilization that was. 
Information is sporadic, tales grow taller each time theyÅfre told, and the language drifts a letter at a 
time.
Å@Å@Å@The current year, in the region of the Great Lakes and little else, is FY 142. FermiÅfs Year is the 
traditional way to mark time, built into the frequent chugs of Stony PointÅfs clock that tells the time to 
the bellowing nuclear facility of the city. Perhaps it was luck that part of the EarthÅfs Blood?the most 
primal of energy?blew a gasket inside the plant. Perhaps it was fate that the Curators were robots 
without a care for the pressure or energy they now produced. It only took a century for a group in this 
broken world to establish a semblance of the Old World.
Å@Å@Å@The Point is the largest city in the region, built to feed off the energy of Stony Point and protect

Å@Å@Å@The Coalition wishes to form a military union?one to protect the people from themselves and

Steel & Wires: Technology
	The Old World was destroyed at the height of its development. Fantastical designs and 
documents point toward what could only be described as fairy tales?flying cars, automated robotics, 
and a nearly limitless amount of resources for everyone to enjoy. Post-Scarcity would be the term 
used, but as with most things, it was built on the backs of the indentured and downtrodden. The haves 
and have-nots were the method by which control was kept and technology was manufactured.
	The technological dark age regressed a majority of humanity's achievements. The processes 
that once enabled the shining cities of the Old World have been replaced with ramshackle proxies and 
an inability to replicate the nuance behind them. Weapons and armor that are now seen as family 
heirlooms were mass-manufactured in the great?now abandoned?factory complexes, and 
communication could once reach across the world with little more than the strength of a radio signal.
	Technology has adapted to the New World, though?human ingenuity is nothing without its 
pride and stubbornness. While the deeper understanding of how the tech was developed or even 
created has been lost, the schematics of how to build it havenÅft. Fragmentary data, mixed with the 
mechanics of today, has created an influx of weapons, armor, and technology designed for the 
modern day rather than the sleek world that came before.
	Weapons and armor have seen the most development and resurgence, with entire companies 
and artisans dedicating their existence to creating the heaviest firepower and most sophisticated 
protection they can?sold to warlord kingdoms and disparate homesteaders alike. ItÅfs necessary, too: 
creatures from beyond the Tears can barely be scratched by rudimentary pipe pistols or crowbars, 
and so the arms race against the apocalypse begins anew.
Vehicles, power armor, and almost everything else have seen some influence from the need to 
militarize the societies that formed during the chaos that followed the collapse of the Old World? 
innovation brought about by conflict, no matter the age.
	Modern technology borrows heavily from the Old World, instead relying on bulkier and less 
efficient methods to produce and manufacture. With interference from more widespread 
infrastructure?Earthblood and other creatures?radio is the only reliable method to speak across 
vast distances. This has led to the control of communication itself: taking one of the radio towers that 
dot the Confederacy or anywhere else in the world is a sure way to hear what everyone is saying, and 
to control what they plan.
	Medically, the regression and subsequent renaissance have been complicated. In the luxurious 
high rises of Stony Point, all it takes is a trip to the medical facility for an Autodoc to diagnose, 
prescribe, and treat any injury someone may have. Further out, a doctor may be little more than a 
local herbalist. The farther one wanders, the less possible serious treatment becomes. The more 
artisanal the skill of doctoring, the more keeping others alive morphs into religious doctrine.
	The development and advancement of the modern world are prefaced by a golden age, a 
dark age that followed, and a drive to survive.

Inland Empire: Psychic 
Å@Å@Å@The mind is the most powerful organ in the human body, able to perform millions of tiny 
calculations in a moment that would shame most supercomputers. Though this is tempered by the 
reality that ÅgBreathingÅh and ÅgBlinkingÅh cut into the potential validity of getting more out of it.. The origin 
of Psychics are shrouded in half-truths and vague documentation from before the collapse of the Old 
World. Trusting those who research Psychoresonant Waves are debatable, most are Psychics 
themselves with an extensive history of being able to perceive and understand the power they wield. 
Historical records are few and far between, mostly being a combination of banal government 
documentation and rants from the unhinged.
Å@Å@Å@Psychics develop young, the most common being in teenagers going through puberty, their 
minds and bodies clicking together to manifest power they donÅft understand. Those who grow up 
around other Psychics are more likely to develop as one themselves, but Null Psychics are only really 
found around high-density psychic communities themselves. Formal training after their Awakening is a 
series of thoughtforms and exercises, trying to ensure that their mind doesnÅft collapse or making them 
believe that the voices in their head are anything but others around them. Though ÅgNatural PsychicsÅh 
born outside enclaves tend to have more of an ad hoc training, either going mad from the voices or 
adopting a disciplined regimen to manifest their power reliably.
Å@Å@Å@After fully developing, Psychics can be found in most levels of society in one way or another. 
Having someone who can read minds or shoot mental energy at their enemies can turn the tide of a 
conflict quickly. Though this doesnÅft mean they are trusted, well tuned Mentalists can read the surface 
thoughts of most people around them, open a secondary mental dialogue with themselves, and even 
possess a weakened mind. To know a Psychic is to learn how to trust someone at a deeper level than 
normal, or putting up the mental guards enough to not worry about trusting another. Though none 
dislike them more than Magicians. The two are one anotherÅfs natural counter, resisting the otherÅfs 
effects far easier than others - eliminating the MagicianÅfs magic forces them to rely on less civilized 
means to put the Psychic in the ground.
Å@Å@Å@Communities of Psychics tend to be small or focused in enclaves of larger settlements. 
Telepathic Psychics are able to communicate with one another wordlessly, creating an eerie silence 
across these districts as the normal bustling sense of conversation is replaced by short nods, off-hand 
snickers, and occasional bursts of verbal anger. These communities are also the only ones able to 
teach young Psychics reliably - which leads to Feral Psychics. ÅgFeral PsychicsÅh is a term to describe 
those who have taught themselves how to manifest their power, often in esoteric or alien methods. 
Dangerous Ferals are the chief reason distrust is as common as it is, but groups of Psychics are known 
to adopt Ferals to add to their breadth of knowledge and abilities to teach. 
Å@Å@Å@In the Great Lakes Confederacy, Stony Point has the largest community of psychics if only due 
to its size. NorthsideÅfs Beach has a sizable retreat of Psychics, though they are divided into different 
schools. The Statesmen are government trained and adopt more practical training regimen, being 
integral to the lawmen and bureaucracy of the Confederacy. The Kai is a doctrine of self-
actualization, becoming ascetics in an effort to both control and manifest their powers. The civil war 
has split these factions further, believing in different doctrines to guide their hand.

Arcana Mystica: Magic
	Magic is the art of using the Earthblood embedded in every person and projecting it outward. 
Earthblood by itself is the volatile substance in which the world is built upon and all matter originates 
from. The end of the Old World was caused by the precise strikes that caused the immense pressure 
of Earthblood to blow, causing the birth of Magic itself. The first magicians were simply born around 
the Earthblood Geysers that sprang up in the aftermath of the collapse and the opening of the Tears - 
their bodies now infused with raw potential energy with nowhere to go. Awakening Magic is a gamble 
depending on where one manages to do it - if they are isolated from others they may find themselves 
burning out before their first year or never understanding the full reason why they have so much 
manic energy. If they are in an environment to know, they are almost always taken away to train 
formally, becoming one of the many types and schools of Magicians out there.
	Awakening oneÅfs Magic is often from birth or soon after, though it has taken others late in their 
teenage years or even their 20s before any hint of the Spark is seen. The Spark is a term used by 
Magicians to recognize the potential in one another, though this may be an adopted term from the 
glimmering effect that oneÅfs aura produces. After developing the Spark, the MagicianÅfs power is 
unpredictable and is prone to firing off when they are stressed or in danger, often itÅfs manyÅfs first 
encounter with it as well. Depending on the Magician and the situation, the training may range 
anywhere from formal institutions that teach the fundamentals, master-apprentice relationships, to 
even little more than philosophical movements haphazardly adopted into becoming magical doctrine.
	Due to Magic being reliant on Earthblood, itÅfs malleable and can be shaped easily through the 
use of a Grimoire - the MagicianÅfs personal shorthand for manifesting their powers. Capable 
Magicians barely need to recite passages or focus themselves, though many more have met an early 
grave by a simple mispronunciation. A Grimoire is a collection of methods to focus and refine oneÅfs 
Magic, it could be an actual book that the Magician must carefully manage, a file on their wrist 
computer, or intricate tattoos on their body. Learning a MagicianÅfs Grimoire lets someone mimic their 
abilities, making protecting it the first thing that an apprentice will learn. After that, Magic Theorem 
and training is all that matters.
	The Magus is the standard term for a Magician, a well rounded and educated individual in their 
arts. Whether this is Algonquin Shamanistic Magic, Aeven Theory, or their own doctrine they have 
sworn themselves too colors and shapes how Magic actually functions. This training and philosophical 
standpoint lets the Magus to twist their magic to their own ends - resulting in further subschools and 
beliefs inside of an already diverse school of thought. As Earthblood is a foundational energy, the 
development of these heuristic shortcuts and mantras can have the same Grimoire manifest different 
spells depending on the Magus employing them. Of course radically different philosophies also crop 
up, using the chaotic force to their own ends.
	Naturally, Magicians loathe being around Psychics.
	The reasons differ, but the two have competing auras that encapsulate their power. Clashes 
break down into fist fights as their magic or psychic powers are rendered moot against one another. 
This has led to frequent Anti-Psychic or Anti-Magic groups that form around any political entity, even 
to the detriment of their own ideology. 
Å@Å@Å@The Great Lakes Confederacy employs Magicians in their ranks, most of them being trained in 
Southside (if only to be away from Psychics). Training tends to be sporadic to the heavily institutional 
Cedar Point Academy, with a few hundred students at any time. Though more Algonquin Shamans 
have begun venturing further into Stony Point to ply their trade. Magicians tend to be wanderers, 
drifting from place to place or working for mercenary companies needing some more magical 
firepower.

Earthblood & Unnatural Phenomenon
	The end of the world was punctuated by a mixture of nuclear hellfire and the last great hurrah 
from great Mother Earth - she bled. Earthblood has been a term being floated around for decades by 
explorers, scholars, and anyone with enough sense to know about it. In basic terms, Earthblood is the 
primal essence of existence, the first ÅgthingÅh that existed and the basis of all of reality. Pouring through 
records and recovering old data troves reveals the closest word to it would be Aether, but even that 
had properties to it, intangible, but ever present. In laymanÅfs language, Earthblood is the blood of the 
Earth keeping the heart, lungs, and brain of the world itself functional. Now that it was torn open, it 
spews out uncontrollably as the Errant Earth either dies squirming or clots itself one day.
	Until then, itÅfs a fact of life.
	Earthblood by its nature is ÅgMore.Åh ItÅfs an excess of life that flourishes everything around it, but 
twists and mangles it at the same time. Dense foliage overruns entire old cities, the water has a 
unnatural hue and invigorating taste, even the animals of yesterday have been enhanced into what 
used to be called ÅgMegafauna.Åh Rapid, divergent, uncontrolled evolution results around the various 
Earthblood wounds that appear. These wounds can be sporadic, an area may become saturated in 
Earthblood causing it to twist and change in a few months before it closes itself - whatever unnatural 
entities that spawned from it adapting to their new reality. This has led to Earthblood Geysers 
appearing in specialized spots - massive spewing bouts of raw energy that if left undirected creates 
an unnatural set of phenomenon and bizarre occurrences.
	One of the stranger expressions of the Earthblood are Leylines, vast stretches of Earthblood 
leaving a ÅgTrailÅh to the next Geyser. Most of the time they are undetectable except to the most 
hardened Magicians - but those who study the Earthblood and its effects can always see the subtle 
signs. This isnÅft implying Magicians donÅft cast an incorrect spell or not think about it, throwing them 
miles away with a bad teleportation or having a fireball explode in the middle of an empty field as the 
Leyline simply ÅgabsorbedÅh the magic to place it elsewhere. Leyline Walkers are able to manipulate 
these, throwing spells and themselves across the vast stretches of the Errant Earth on the highways of 
reality. 
	Why hasnÅft humanity or civilization crumbled in the aftermath of these ripping apart the old 
world? They did, for a time. Earthblood is natural though, something that flows perfectly fine on its 
own and doesnÅft struggle to create whatÅfs already natural. Humanity has perfected the art of the 
unnatural, preferring to tame the world than live in harmony with it. Crafted from alloys, false metals, 
and manufactured goods, itÅfs mused that humanity was the perfect opposing force to Earthblood. 
Raw Earthblood hates urbanized, metallic, or ÅgunnaturalÅh places - what power it can manifest there is 
little more than a flicker compared to one of their smallest open wounds. 
	This hasnÅft stopped humanity from harnessing this power, those exposed to it may have the 
spark of magic embedded in their souls, rapid onset mutations are often due to it, and even those who 
feed on the latent energy follow the wounds and ride the waves they create. One day humanity will 
need to live without this power, this raw expression of life that burns within the veins of the world, but 
today is not that day.

The Tears
Å@Å@Å@Earthblood isnÅft the only mysterious oddity that occurred, perhaps due to the influx of that raw 
energy and connections to other pockets of existence, lead to the Tears opening up. Tears are 
anomalies to all those except the wisest and more experienced, but the laymen know one thing - 
Tears cause others to come through. The difficulty of discussing Tears is due to the infinite realities 
that they open up to and the explanation others give for why. A Tear may open for day on the Errant 
Earth but be reported to be opened for a century on the other side, other times a glowing pillar of light 
that has been part of the natural landscape since the Collapse sporadically throws unfortunates into

Å@Å@Å@Tears open a portal, often one way, to the Errant Earth from ÅgOtherÅh places. Sometimes other 
humans come through, displaced and mystified about the world, abducted gunslingers meet veterans 
from ancient wars, only to be hired together by a field agent from a different worldline entirely. But 
the ÅgExosÅh are the most common. Exo is part identifier, part slur, for displaced groups and societies

cosmos only to find themselves lost in this foreign world. Others are more fantastical, straight out of a

Å@Å@Å@Those who have been stranded for years have adapted to their new home. Generations of

already called to question. Periods of peace will be punctuated by an invasion by a foreign species,

color and reason linger, only for them to creep into a world of distorted shapes and incorrect 
vibrations that they seek to cleanse.
Å@Å@Å@The Errant Earth is home to many strangers. Whether they are friend or enemy is for the one 
holding the gun to decide. 

The Drifters
Å@Å@Å@Drifters are by their nature a transitory people - driven from their homes by either a burning 
wanderlust, fortunate circumstances, or the needs of others. Drifters wander, finding themselves in the 
Errant EarthÅfs many curiosities and problems. Many pursue higher ambitions, some may be simply to

power that seems to reach out to them.
Å@Å@Å@Drifters are never quite at home anywhere - strangers in a strange land that band together not 
necessarily out of obligation or desire, but mutual protection. One may dislike the hulking brute who 
canÅft speak their language well and drools after any meat, but appreciating them ripping a raging 
mutant in half is always good.

Great Lakes Confederacy
	 The formation of the Great Lakes Confederacy began when the Fermi Brotherhood formally 
established the community around what would gradually be known as Stony Point. Stony Point is a 
nuclear reactor in which a Earthblood Wound opened up in, rather than cause damage or mutate the 
surroundings, the immortal and robotic caretakers simply integrated it into the system and spiked 
power output to ludicrous levels. The Fermi Brotherhood began exploiting the power and eventually 
Stony Point became a town, then a city, then the sprawling metropolis it is today.
	The nominal head of the Confederacy is the Council of Seven, ten members democratically 
elected to manage the day-to-day operations alongside the Lower Chambers of a hundred different 
individuals with some democratic seats and other established seats for important groups in society. As 
Stony Point grew it reached out to other communities in the area, offering power and their expertise 
in exchange for whatever they could offer. The first major alliance was with Chigeon, the mutant and 
exo filled community in the ruins of Old Chicago - namely the Grand Diocese of Chigeon and the 
Regent of St. Peter. Expanding further and further until most of the Great Lakes Region had some kind 
of affiliation with Stony Point and the Lower Chambers became further bloated with alliance 
members and allies to the Fermi Brotherhood and the power plant. 
	This lasted for around fifty years before tensions began to arise - different members of the 
Confederacy began accusing others of Ågtaking more than their dueÅh and after the Canadian War a 
decade ago, all civility broke down and the Confederacy was split between the Coalition and the 
Union.
	The Coalition is based around Saint Marie on the border of the Canadians - originally a 
militarized society, they saw the worst fighting of the Canadian War and they gradually became 
disenfranchised by the ÅgWeakÅh further south. The Coalition boasts a strong military and allies within 
Stony Point itself - their continued war against ÅgThe OthersÅh has turned to fascist rhetoric. They are led 
by Grand Marshal Furio, a dour and angry man who has grand ambitions of turning the Confederacy 
into his own personal empire. Though Furio is often undermined by his own minions trying to earn his 
favor, earn their own petty ranks and honors, or trying to usurp the Grand Marshal himself. Without this 
inefficiency at the top ranks of society, the Coalition could probably sweep the Confederacy entirely - 
but holding it would be a different story?
	The UnionÅfs base of operation is Buffalo Falls, though their allies take up a majority of the Lake 
Ontario region as well as those few who remain affiliated with them in Stony Point. What the Union 
lacks in conventional military they make up for in a host of artists, exos, psychics, and ÅgOthersÅh that are 
demeaned by others. Not to say that the Union is unified in any way. Different groups rally together to 
oppose the Coalition, not to support one another. Haphazard Militias are more likely to fight among 
themselves than lead a consistent fight against their ideological enemy. Leading to the Union 
leadership employing adventurers and drifters to do a majority of the work.
	The future of Stony Point and the Confederacy is in the balance - ChigeonÅfs mounting unrest 
between the two forces are reaching a boiling point, skirmishes in the East are escalating into full 
blown battles, and hungry eyes of the enemies of the Confederacy seem to seeing if this moment of 
weakness is the time to decapitate their ancient enemy.

Drifting Vagabonds
Å@Å@Å@Errant Earth is a roleplaying game about the adventures and struggles of a disparate group of 
Drifters in a wild and twisted Earth far after the Collapse destroyed it. With the opening of the Tears 
and Earthblood Geysers - high technology, powerful magic, weird psychics, and other Exos that find 
themselves on the Errant Earth, the struggle to survive mixes with the strange and wonderful from 
places-beyond-places.
	A group of Players, or PL, will become a set of Drifters. These men and women find themselves 
wandering the Errant Earth in search of their own ends - whether this is fame, fortune, destiny, or the 
will to make a difference is up to them. They will need to manage their resources, allies, and skills in the 
field to make their mark, or they may end up joining many who could not. One of these players will be 
the Game Master, or GM. As the Game Master, their role is to be the narrator of events and act on 
behalf of the ensemble cast the Drifters will encounter in peace and war. They will place challenges 
and situations in front of the Drifters, forcing these wayward children of the apocalypse to overcome 
or succumb to them. 
	Errant Earth uses the D20/100 System and is played with a full set of dice from D4 to D20. 
Whenever a Drifter attempts an action with a chance of failure or is in direct opposition to another, 
they will perform a Check to see if they succeed or fail. The GM will declare the Check to be an 
Attribute or Skill Check, but a clever Drifter may propose alternatives to the situation they find 
themselves in.
 
	Attribute Checks are called when the Drifter must rely on brute forcing the situation or relying 
on their personal abilities rather than any formal training. They will take a twenty-sided die, or D20, 
and attempt to roll under their Attribute.
	If they roll under their Attribute Score, they are successful and manage to bypass the situation. 
If they roll over their Attribute Score, they fail and suffer the consequences. 

A Drifter needs to pull themselves up on a ledge, they roll against the Power Attribute to pull 
themselves up. Failure has them struggle to climb up and waste time in the attempt.

Å@Å@Å@Skill Checks are called when the Drifter is using their training or skills to attempt to overcome a 
problem. They will take two ten-sided dice (d10) and roll them together. One die will record the 10's 
place while the other records the 1's place  - this is called making a Percentile, or D100, roll.
	If the Drifter rolls under their Skill, they are successful and manage to work out how to solve the 
situation. if they roll over their Skill, they fail and suffer complications that may arise. 

A Drifter is scouting the nearby woodland area, they'll be rolling a Wilderness Survival check. With 
their Wilderness Survival at 43, they manage to score a 12, succeeding at the Check.

?
Opposed Checks
	Whenever the Drifter is being directly opposed by another individual or group, both parties will 
be making a Check to determine the victor. Both groups will be making the same type of Check unless 
specified, and whoever is victorious wins the day. It is entirely possible for both sides to emerge 
victorious, in this case, whoever has the highest result will manage to overcome their opponent. For 
example, if a Drifter rolls a 43 and succeeds, if their opponent rolls a 42 or less, no matter if they 
succeed or not, they will still lose the competition.
Å@Å@Å@If both sides fail their Check, they will roll again with a -2 / -10% until one either runs out of their 
ability to act or someone manages to succeed. If both parties are particularly skilled or their Attributes 
are large, they will use the 20/100 Rule instead. If one or both parties exceed 20 in Attributes, they will 
both apply a penalty until the highest Attribute is a 20 and then roll. In addition, if one or both parties 
exceed 100 in a Skill, they will apply a penalty until it is only 100.
 
Two Drifters are locked in an arm wrestling 
match, both roll their Power Attribute. One Drifter 
successfully rolls a 5 and the other a 19 - the 
Drifter with 19 fails the Check and loses the 
competition.
Two Drifters are competing against one another 
in a race. Both will roll their Ground Vehicle 
Piloting Skill. Both of the Drifters succeed at their 
Check, but one rolls a 23 and the other a 32 - the 
32 wins.
 
A Drifter is challenged to a drinking contest with a 
Mutant with Supernatural Hardiness of 23, while 
they only have a 15. The Mutant imposes a -3 to 
both their own and the DrifterÅfs Hardiness (20 vs 
12) before the Opposed Check begins. The Drifter 
rolls an 11, but the Mutant scores a 16 and drinks 
them under the table after a few rounds. 
A Drifter is attempting to defeat a rival in a 
musical contest - they have a Musical Instrument 
Skill of 125 and their opponent has 150. Both incur 
the -50 Penalty for a 75 vs 100 Skill Check. The 
Drifter scores a 68 while their opponent manages 
to roll a 13 - the Drifter successfully beats the 
superior foe, if only barely. 


The Wayward Notes: Combat	
During Combat, the Drifters will be making D20 
Checks to hit their enemies, rather than rolling 
under, combat in Errant Earth and the D20/100 
System is against a Target Number, requiring 
the Drifter to roll over to beat it. This is 
expanded out and thoroughly explained in the 
Combat Chapter. 

Confederate Records: Rounding
All instances of Rounding will be rounded up, so 
2.5 would be 3, with 2.3 also being 3. If this isnÅft 
the case, it will be noted.

Saves
	During their encounters on the Errant 
Earth, the Drifters will occasionally need to 
protect themselves from threats that are not 
immediately physical. A "Save" is an Attribute 
Check that allows the Drifter to resist the 
effects of certain abilities used on them.
	If the Save is Successful, the effect is 
mitigated or halved in effectiveness - if the 
Save Fails then the Drifter experiences the full 
consequences. 
Difficulty Rating
	Situations on the Errant Earth can be hectic and often dangerous, whenever a complication or 
boon is affecting the Drifter they will be using a Difficulty Rating. Difficulty Ratings are bonuses and 
penalties applied to the Drifter's Check should they attempt it. These are always considered to be 
"exterior" factor, often related to the environment, other people, or the situation in front of them rather 
than their own personal skill.
Å@Å@Å@Difficulty Ratings are judged as "One" - meaning that if the Drifter has a +30% ease, a -20% later 
on would make the final calculation a +10% instead.

Defaulting
	Whenever a Drifter does not have a Skill appropriate to the 
situation, they may instead attempt to Default to one of their 
Attributes. When Defaulting, the Drifter will multiply the appropriate 
Attribute by the current Difficulty of the Check. They will then make a 
Skill Check instead of the Attribute Check.
	For example, if a Drifter is Defaulting to an Attribute of 12 with 
only Average Complexity, they will need to make a Skill Check with a 
Target Number of 24 (12 Attribute x 2 Complexity).
	Not every Skill may have the Drifter Default, the Game Master 
has the final say on what is, and is not, appropriate for the Drifter to 
attempt a Default Check on. If the Drifter does succeed at a Defaulted 
Skill Check, the Success should be less ÅgknowhowÅh and more related to 
either luck or it being the minimum viable success. Failing a Defaulted 
Check is often a similar, or more gradoise failure due to not knowing 
what's actually going wrong.

The 99/00 & Skills Over 100%
	Whenever the Drifter is making a Skill Check, a roll of 99 or 100 will always result in Failure, no 
matter how high the Skill is. This represents the quirks of fate interfering with the Drifter's plans, such 
as unexpected complications or unlucky happenstance. Skills can reach over 100%, meaning that they 
can only fail with the 99/00, but they will be able to blunt any complications that may occur to 
maintain their two-percent margin of error. 
Damage Scaling [M6]
	Errant Earth is considered to be an M6 Setting. This means it is a Megacapable Setting with 
Mega Damage (MD) being recorded normally and potentially lethally. If the Drifters were to ever take 
Giga or Ultra Damage, they will not record it and instead be immediately vaporized or annihilated by 
the titanic attack.

Drifter Creation
	The Errant Earth is host to a plethora of souls from all walks of life. The path of the Drifter 
doesn't discriminate and many find themselves taking up the wayward lifestyle for their own reasons. 
The quintessential Drifter is a wanderer, someone who rolls into a community to do some work before 
leaving again. The term has morphed and changed over the years, some taking it as a mark of pride 
of their nomadic lifestyle, others viewing it as an demeaning insult to their new situation.
	Regardless of the reason why they are drifting, each one has the knowhow to survive and will 
be making a name for themselves - whether they like to or not. 

Attributes
	Attributes represent a set of basic qualifications for the Drifter and their natural perspective on 
their lifestyle after they have begun their new life. These are intrinsic parts of the Drifter and will 
inform large parts of their actions, choices, and abilities throughout their allies. Attributes will rarely 
change afte they have been determined, only being modified after augmentation, ATB (Attribute 
Bonus) Skills, or relying on the quirks of fate that seem to follow them. Of course, oneÅfs Attributes may 
also fall due to horrific injury or other debilitating effects.
	To determine one's Attributes, the Drifter will take the three dice gained from their 
Backgrounds and Occupations - rolling them together to determine their final result. The natural 
Mortal limit of Attributes is 18, a quintessential person with heroic disposition. Though Attributes can 
also dip a low as 3 normally, representing severe handicaps or issues affecting the Drifter's personal 
life.
	Errant Earth has six scales to represent how modified a Drifter is in regards to their Attributes. 
These six scales represent how high the Drifter's Attribute potential is, as well as how they appear to a 
majority of others.

Background & Occupations
	Every Drifter has a story to tell. With each of these stories they always tend to be the 
protagonist of their own heroic fantasy or rather miserable experience. 
	Each Drifter has Backgrounds and Occupations which define their initial skill set, physical 
features, and attributes they have. Normally a Drifter has three: Background, Occupation, and one of 
their choice. Specialized Drifters only have a Background and Occupation. Each different Background 
and Occupation has their own separate set of benefits and drawbacks associated with them, with the 
Drifter being able to improve them gradually.
	Whenever the Drifter has reached a milestone in their life, they will increase their Character 
Level, or CL, by one. CL indicates the overall experience of the Drifter in the field, thus a "CL 5" Drifter is 
more experienced than a "CL 1" Drifter. Increasing a CL allows the Drifter to increase the Rank of all of 
their currently acquired Backgrounds and Occupations, increasing their Rank by 1 . Specialized 
Drifters may add two Ranks to their Occupation or Background, alternating between the two . 
	Background and Occupation features may be measured by Character Level or Rank. Every CL 
5 is every five Character Levels, while Rank 5, indicates that it must be at least Rank 5 or greater. 
Increasing CL directly increases each Background and Occupation, so why the difference?
	Drifters may transfer out of Backgrounds and Occupations during different intervals in their life. 
Representing a part of their life that no longer defines them or is stagnating them. Once a Background 
or Occupation is transferred out of, the Drifter may not "re-enter" the Background or Occupation. 
Though they will keep all of the bonuses (and drawbacks) they would have acquired from their time. 
	Different Backgrounds and Occupations will have a different amount of Karma they have 
access to. Karma is gained every CL equal to the Karma ratings of all current Backgrounds and 
Occupations. This allows the Drifter to further develop themselves outside of the rigidity of their 
Background or Occupation. High Karma indicates an adaptable and open ended approach, while low 
(or negative!) Karma is rigid and strict in how it develops properly .?

Adonis (Racial)
Clones, Meatmen, Legionnaires, Samefaces, Bucketheads
	The Adonis is a simple creature, their ÅgPeopleÅh are Homo Perfectus, the perfect specimen of 
humanity synthesized in an ancient lab to be cloned en masse to wage war in the name of whoever 
paid their bills. That history ended with the Collapse - the renegade Adonis of a world that ceased to 
be kept doing what they did best: fight. Endlessly cloning themselves in their facilities to continue the

Åú	Magical Artifact - The Artifact is magical in nature,

Åú	Psychic Artifact - The Artifact radiates a

the Drifter acquires a Psychic Skill to use. If taken 
during Drifter Creation - it possesses 2 Psychic Skills 
of Choice.

Two Souls - The Artifact is symbiotic with the Drifter, feeding 
off one another for immediate survival or power. The Drifter 
creates their ESP or MP Pool as normal, even if they donÅft have 
awakened Magic or Psychic Powers. When using Spells or 
Psychic Abilities, the Drifter will use this pool to use it.

+1d10 as its power grows. If the Drifter were to awaken their

Åú	Magical Artifacts - Find someone able to use Sealing

Åú	Psychic Artifacts - The Drifter must enter the Inland

decides when the Drifter is allowed in (or is forced

Attribute.
	Full Conversion Borgs have replaced a majority of their body 
with Cybernetics, leading to being barely human to begin with. They 
are considered to be MD Capable as their skin is entirely metallic with 
their Finesse, Hardiness, Power, and Speed being Mechanical with a 
[D6] Cybernetic Enhancement.

Cybernetic enhancements.

The Withdrawal-  When the Drifter misses their Juice hit, 
theyÅfll enter Withdrawal. There are four stages of Withdrawal:

Vampiris

Light
Demeanor is considered four steps worse than normal.
Heavy

to be at half their regular value.
Crippling

who is bleeding.

Turbo

Light

Heavy

it 0, set it to .25 instead.
Crippling
The Drifter loses the ability to walk unassisted. 

JAX

Light
Every missed dose deals 3d6 SD directly to Endurance 
and then Health.
Heavy
All Physical Actions are considered to be at -8 / -40% 
until a dose is taken.
Crippling
The Drifter enters a coma for 1d6 Days.

JAX

Light
-5 / -25% to all Actions as their limbs grow heavy and 
perception becomes unfocused.
Heavy
Lose all Weapon Proficiencies and Weapon 
Specializations due to chemical imbalances. 
Crippling
Endurance is set to 0 and cannot increase.

The Detox -   Once the Drifter has  gotten past the Crippling 
Withdrawal Effect, they are able to function normally enough 
and begin the Detox process. Detoxing fully takes (1d6 x Juice 
Addiction) Days to process. Until then, they must contend with 
the Light Withdrawal Condition only. If they successfully Detox, 
they are able to Transfer out of the Background.

Spartan (Trait)
Soldier Boys, Hardhats, Bloodgulchers
	The Spartan Procedure takes place over the course of three days. The first day is a cocktail of 
drugs and stimulants to open every kind of pain receptor, sense, and overall aptitude the recipient has. 
The second is the invasive cybernetic procedure to replace various internal organs with their 
enhanced SPARTAN variant to keep their body functional and enhance their physical abilities. The

rapidfire combat simulations through the exhausted mind of the agonized recipient. Few survive the 
full procedure, fewer come out as they were. What remains is a SPARTAN, a person molded into 
becoming a quintessential killer, their minds scrambled and replaced with little more than killing intent.
	Spartans arenÅft made for everyone, those who undertake the procedure serve their tenure in 
militaries or find themselves battling in Splurgoth Slave Pits until they free themselves. Their bodies are 
molded to kill, their minds honed to a knifeÅfs edge, a darkness behind their eyes. Power comes at a 
price, and many argue a Spartan has no soul.

	People run from their past, often faster with each step they take. But no matter what, their past 
is always catching up to them - often in the shape of a Hunter. Hunters venture out to find their targets 
and bring them back. Bounty Hunters track men, Monster Hunters track monsters, and Witch Hunters 
find the wicked and evil - every society has found the use of Hunters in them, though their profession is 
often distasteful to many. An essential part of society, yet ostracized from it for the exact reason their 
society calls upon them. A paradoxical career choice.
	Hunter Drifters are just living their natural endpoint, wandering justicars or murderers finding 
their endless quarries in a long string of jobs. Does society need them, or do they need society? 
Perhaps neither, perhaps both. A paradoxical outcome.

Infiltrator (Man-At-Arms)
Spy, Assassin, Hired Gun, Commando, Black Ops, Spooks
	Combat is about three things - knowing more than the enemy, overpowering the enemy, and 
only fighting when you absolutely know you can win. Infiltrators have a number of names, but they 
specialize in the acquisition and information of the core tenants of combat. Preferring to work alone or 
in small teams, Infiltrators rely less on raw combat ability and more on their ability to avoid fighting all 
together. Infiltrators can also be less organized, haphazard breaking & entering specialists with 
enough combat experience to make it out if it does go wrong.
	Infiltrators becoming Drifters is often a necessary evil for them, sometimes they learn too much 
and itÅfs the 9mm retirement plan, other times their work becomes too hard on the soul and they take 
to the road to ease their troubled heart. Of course others pick up the tricks, a valuable commodity in a 
world where there are haves and have nots.

Initial Karma
	Karma is the measure of the weight of oneÅfs soul, the experiences both good and bad, and the 
drive to make a change in themselves and the world around them. In Errant Earth, Karma is the 
measure of adaptability that a Drifter has during their life. Karma is built up from each of the 
Backgrounds and Occupations that the Drifter has, being acquired and built up across their 
experiences.
	The DrifterÅfs initial Karma may be spent to acquire new Skills and abilities for the Drifter, 
enabling them to be better and shape their destiny more than those who have little Karma. As the 
Drifter increases their Character Level, they will be able to use their Karma more to improve 
themselves, but at a slower and costly rate. During this initial expenditure of Karma, the DrifterÅfs 
weight is being lifted off their shoulders as they go adventuring. Any remaining Karma is added to the 
DrifterÅfs total Karma for improvements.

Extra Sensory Power / Magic Power
Drifters who are capable of using Psychic Powers 
or Magic possess Extra Sensory Power (ESP) or 
Magic Power (MP).
ESP is the measure of control that a Drifter has 
over their Psychic Powers and abilities. When 
actively using them, the Drifter reduces their 
available ESP until they are able to rest.
MP is the amount of power that a Drifter has to 
use and project their Magical abilities. Whenever 
they use Magical Abilities or wish to enhance 
them, they will be tapping into their MP, restoring 
it when they are able to rest.

Drifters who are exceptionally talented 
Magicians or Psychics can inherently protect 
themselves better against their diametric foe 
easier than most.
The Psychic / Magic Resistance bonus is 
generated when a Drifter unlocks their Psychic or 
Magical Potential - granting them extra defense 
against their opposite force. This is directly 
added to an Attribute when a Psychic or Magic 
Save is called to resist their effects.

Psychic Resistance is based on Willpower
Magic Resistance is based on Anima.

Packs & Credits
	When the Drifter chooses their Background and Occupations they will have access to a number 
of Packs and their starting Credits. Packs are a set of items and gear that the Drifter may pick up with 
useful supplies for their journey. A Drifter may select one Packs of their choice of any of their 
Backgrounds and Occupations they have access to. Drifters may instead exchange a Pack for Credits 
instead, often less than the total amount but being able to purchase what they wish.
	Finally, each Drifter has a set of starting Credits from their Backgrounds and Occupations. The 
Drifter adds all of their available Credits from each of the Backgrounds and Occupations they have. 
They may choose to save these or spend them in the equipment section.

New World Bible - Credits & Currency
Money makes the world go round, and the Great Lakes Confederacy needed to establish a base 
currency for their new ÅgFederation.Åh The GLC, Great Lakes Credit, is technically a digital currency 
with a backing of the energy of Stony Point, making it a popular coin for most people in the region. 
Actual ÅgCurrencyÅh is still used, basic script, sparkly coins, scrap, or whatever can be used to indicate 
value. The barter economy is still actively used in most places.

Background Occupation Mergers
	During their creation, the Drifter may acquire several skills or abilities that cross over with one 
another. Taking all of these abilities and merging them together is as simple as following this chart. 
The Best Variant refers to the Background or Occupation with the highest starting Development Rate 
(Hobby, Trained, or Core) or the highest quality (Military Combat Training vs Basic Combat Training). 
If the Drifter has chosen Skills as part of a Background or Occupation, such as Professional, they may 
apply these bonuses as well.

Endurance and Health
	Drifters have an unnatural belief that they are in fact immortal, something that is written on 
more epitaphs than one would think. Drifters get hurt, bloodied, maimed, and most other kinds of 
trauma the Errant Earth has to offer. To reflect the DrifterÅfs ability to absorb and take punishment, 
they have their total Endurance and Health.
	A DrifterÅfs Endurance measures their ability to shrug off injury, the near misses, scratches, 
bruises, and flesh wounds that stack up before they take the debilitating injuries tied to their Health. 
When Endurance reaches 0, the Drifter's Health will start being targeted, should they reach 0 Health, 
the Drifter will be killed. 

Endurance
2d6  + HRD (+1d4 / CL)
Health
HRD

Å@Å@Å@A Drifter will recover their Endurance after being able to rest for the night or being patched up 
in a medical tent. A normal human being will recover +1 Health every day, and +2 Health if they are 
under medical care. 
	If a Drifter would fall below 0 Health, they may instead take a Scar. Scars mitigate the damage 
they would have taken, but cause a permanent injury. Scars may be expressed as a -1 to an Attribute 
or narrative debilitation  (often requiring surgery or cybernetics to mitigate the loss of a limb or 
worse). If a Drifter were to ever take 5 or more Scars of any variety, they will be immediately 
removed from play due to the severe injuries and trauma they have endured.
 
	Endurance and Health are both considered to be Standard Damage meaning that if they are 
hit with a Mega Damage Weapon, it is immediately reduced to 0 (potentially fatal or risking an arm). If 
a Drifter would ever be considered to be a Mega Damage Capable individual through Mutations, 
Cybernetics, or their own physiology, then their Endurance and Health would work normally upon 
being hit with Mega Damage Weaponry - not being able to be pierced except by excessive varieties 
by Standard Damage sources however.
	To mitigate this, the survivors of the Collapse have retrofitted old designs and made their own 
new armors and weapons in the ancient arms race of armor and weaponry. Most Armor is 
considered to be Mega Damage capable except in deliberate circumstances. This is all a casual way 
to remind every Drifter, no matter how brave or mighty - always take care of your armor.
?
Skills
	Skills represent a host of knowledge, talents, and abilities that a Drifter has developed or picked 
up over the years through their education, life experiences, and natural development. Each Drifter has 
a number of Skills determined by their Backgrounds and Occupations, split up Core, Trained, Hobby, 
Perfect, ATB, Combat Training, Weapon Proficiencies, and Combat Specialties.
	Core, Trained, and Hobby Skills are the sliding scale of in depth information of focus the Drifter 
has placed on different skills. Core Skills are fundamental to the DrifterÅfs life and training, developing 
faster than their Trained Skills. Hobby Skills develop slowly, and sometimes not at all, as they are 
picked up aspects rather than developed talents. Perfect Skills are those which are innate to the 
Drifter and nearly impossible to fail unless in dire circumstances or extreme complications - such as 
being able to speak their native language or know about where they grew up.
Å@Å@Å@These Skills follow the same format with a [Base Skill Value] + [Development]. 
Å@Å@Å@The Base Skill indicates what the Skill begins at when it is first opened by the Drifter. For 
example, the Investigation Skill has a Base Skill Value of 35%. The Development of the Skill is the 
percentage next to it that indicates its growth everytime the Drifter increases their Character Level. 
The Investigation Skill has a Trained Development of +7% - so if a Drifter has the Investigation Skill at 
35% and increases their Character Level, they would now have 42% as their Investigation Skill. 
Å@Å@Å@During Drifter Creation, each of the Drifters will apply their Development when their Skill is first 
opened up . If the Drifter opens a Skill up later through either spending Karma, Learning 
Opportunities, or Education - they will begin at the Base Skill Value and begin improving the next 
Character Level.
Å@Å@Å@Core, Trained, and Hobby Skills will indicate the rate of development for the Drifters. Core 
Skills develop the fastest, with Hobby Skills developing the slowest. Improving and refining Skills later 
on, such as promoting a Hobby Skill into a Trained Skill, would improve the Development but not make 
up Åglost experienceÅh of previous levels. After a Skill reaches 100%, Development slows dramatically, as 
the Drifter is no longer learning how to improve themselves, but instead refining their craft to avoid or 
mitigate potential disasters. 
Å@Å@Å@ATB, Combat Training, Weapon Proficiencies, and Combat Specialties do not have a [Base 
Skill] or [Development], instead when they acquire this Skill they will have all of the benefits it entails 
immediately. ATB, or Attribute Bonus, Skills improve the DrifterÅfs Attributes through rigorous 
commitment or focus, but do little else outside of it. Combat Training is how skilled the Drifter is in 
combat, directly correlating to a number of Combat Actions they have. Possessing a Weapon 
Proficiency allows a deeper understanding of particular weapons for special combat actions. A 
Combat Speciality is an art that the Drifter has developed to improve their combat ability, but not 
directly correlate to an increase in actions or immediate weapon benefits. 

The Wayward Notes	- ÅgUse AsÅh
The Game Master may allow the Drifter to use one skill ÅgasÅh another. Most Skills do not allow this by 
their nature - but various mechanics and other details may assist. If this is the case, it will either half 
the value of the Skill for the attempt or take a penalty of -20 / -40 / -60% as normal.

	During the DrifterÅfs life and their adventures 
on the Errant Earth, they may begin to internalize 
deeper meanings to their Skills and start applying 
Skill Tags. A Skill Tag is a refinement of the SkillÅfs 
abilities and nature, improving them or allowing 
the Drifter to perform tricks to keep them ahead 
or enable them to push beyond their limits.
	Each Skill may take as many Skill Tags that 
are applied to them, with each possessing a 
different function. Particular Drifters may even be 
a master in several Skills with all of the proper Skill 
Tags and abilities.

The Wayward Notes - Special Benefits of Skill Acquisition
Certain Backgrounds or Occupations may possess a Skill written as [Skill (+10%)] or similar. This 
indicates that the Drifter will add an immediate +10% bonus to the Base Skill Value when they open 
the Skill. 
Later on through dedication, education, or other Ågless savoryÅh techniques the Drifter may gain a flat 
bonus to a Skill as well. This is added directly onto the Base Skill Value. 

The Wayward Notes - Open Skills
An Open Skill refers to a broad skill set that covers many different fields. Rather than have an 
individual entry for each of them, an Open Skill may take its palace. When the Drifter takes an Open 
Skill, they will define what it actually is for purposes of refinement. The Natural Sciences is an Open 
Skill - allowing the Drifter to have Natural Sciences: Biology or Natural Sciences: Chemistry based on 
their preferences. The Drifter may take multiple of the same type of Open Skill if they wish, allowing 
them to be multi-disciplined inside of a singular field. 
The Game Master has the final call in regards to what are appropriate Open Skills.
?

Confederate Records - Skill Development Index
The Skill Development Index is a personal system to determine how Skills are built using the Base 
Skill Value, Development, and such. Every Skill is placed on an imaginary 4x4 matrix of Difficulty of 
the Skill and the Learning Complexity of the Skill. The Difficulty is how immediately complicated or 
strange the skill is - Electronic Warfare has a Base Skill Value of 20% due to it being a specialist skill. 
The Learning Complexity is how gradual one can develop and learn about the Skill over time, the 
Disguise Skill is easy to learn (+7% Trained) due to its nature.
Thus a Skill thatÅfs ÅgSimple to learn, Hard to MasterÅh (Simple Specialist Skill) would be 50% + 3% (50% 
Base Skill Level + 3% Development at Trained).

The Wayward Notes - Field vs Garage Repairs
When a Drifter needs to make repairs they will either be repairing in 
the field or at a garage. 
Field Repairs are ÅgDefaultÅh assuming the Drifter has the appropriate 
tools on them. If they donÅft they may still attempt with a [-40%]. 
Successful Field Repairs restore +1d6 Hull Damage.
Garage Repairs are when all the necessary supplies, tools, and space is 
available for the mechanic. They may add +40% to their Skill or 
attempt a similar Skill Check but restore +3d6 Hull Damage.

The Wayward Notes - ÅgNuanceÅh Skills
A ÅgNuanceÅh Skill is a Technical Skill that a Drifter may take to 
ÅgSpecializeÅh one of their other Skills. A Skill Such as 
Computer Use could have a Nuance Skill of ÅgComputer 
Hacking.Åh 
These start and develop at the Technical SkillÅfs rate. 
However, the ÅgCapÅh to this Skill is equal to its Parent Skill 
current cap. Thus if Computer Use is at 75% then Computer 
Hacking can only raise to 75% no matter what. 
Nuance Skills will grant a ÅgBetterÅh outcome than using the 
Parent Skill.
Why is this a side note? It is bulkier and more awkward, use 
at your own peril.

Weapon Proficiencies
	Each Weapon Proficiency Skill may only be taken once. If the Drifter does not have the Weapon 
Proficiency, they may still use the weapon, but not perform any Weapon Expertise with it. The Archaic 
Projectile Weapons, Archaic Melee Weapons, and Archaic Firearms cover all weapons in regards to 
their standard damage variants - all other Combat Proficiencies are considered to be for Mega 
Damage melee weapons or firearms.

Weapon Specialties
	A Weapon Specialty is a refinement of a Drifter's combat abilities that are not directly 
impacting their  quality of combat training. Each Specialty allows the Drifter to have different options 
or bonuses under specific circumstances. Each Weapon Specialty may only be taken once, but its 
effects will apply to all weapons or actions that fit under it.

Warfare on Errant Earth
	Bloodshed has been part of human history as long as there has been history, and when the 
Tears ripped apart the world after the first manmade apocalypse many thought it would be the end. 
Unfortunately, warfare is human. The Errant Earth is filled with monsters, cyborgs, mutants, bandits, 
and militaries who wage a never ending war against one another for survival. While many would 
rather avoid it, the Drifter's life is rarely free of conflict, often finding themselves in the heart of a battle 
with little more than their wits, damaged armor, and a loaded rifle. 
	During combat in Errant Earth, the Drifters will be using a combination of Attribute, Skill, and 
Combat Checks to win the day. A Combat Check uses a D20 with the Drifter attempting to beat their 
target's Survival Rating to hit and deal damage. Rather than a traditional Attribute Check, the Combat 
Check sees if the Drifter manages to meet or exceed the Survival Rating of their target - though this 
does allow them to modify their chances and also avoid any retaliation that may be coming for them.

Seizing the Initiative
	When a combat situation occurs, all of the Drifters and their enemies will need to roll their 
Initiative to determine their Action Order. The Action order resolves in descending order, with the 
highest result acting first and lowest acting last.	

1d20 + [Reaction Modifier] + [Modifiers]

	When a Drifter's Initiative is called, they will be able to take a Turn, allowing them to use their 
Actions gained through their Combat Training. All of the combatant's Turns compose a Round, with 
each of these Rounds being broken up into roughly ten-seconds of frantic movement, quick shots, and 
haphazard plans. 
	If the Drifters were to ambush the opposing group, each of the Drifters would roll their Initiative 
and determine their Acting Order as usual. However, their enemies would be unable to take any 
Actions or Reactions during this Ambush if they are surprised, rolling for their Initiative at the start of 
the next Round and slot themselves into the Acting Order alongside the Drifters. If the Drifters were to 
set themselves up in a clearly defensible position with a kill zone and lines of fire, the same event will 
occur except for the defending side, allowing the Drifters to take a few potshots and actions against 
the assaulting enemy force. 

The Wayward Notes - An ÅgRealÅh Example
A group of bandits are camped far outside the town where the Drifters were hired to stop them, meandering around the campfire with a few of them 
still armed and patrolling, but unaware of the danger. If the DrifterÅfs open up fire on the unaware enemy - they have Ambushed them.
Later on, for retaliation against their group that was cut down, the Bandit Leader sends his entire gang after the town. Being able to hold the line with 
their rudimentary defenses, the Drifters have a Defensive Position, and are able to crack a few shots off on the approaching horde. 
 
Both of these situations would allow the Drifters an initial set of Actions against their enemies and potentially turn the tide. 
But remember, this may also happen to the Drifters.
?
Natural & Mechanized Survival Rating
	During combat the Drifter will be maneuvering frantically looking for cover or attempting to 
position themselves for the decisive blow. What determines their ability to avoid the hospital or an 
early grave, as well as determine their ability to strike an enemy in retaliation is measured by their 
Survival Rating.
	Natural Survival Rating (NSR) is the standard difficulty to strike an aware combatant who is not 
actively in cover or seeking to defend themselves actively. The NSR rating is determined by the size of 
the individual representing how difficult it is to pinpoint a shot on them as they scramble to avoid 
injury. Whenever a Drifter is attempting to attack an enemy, they will need to meet or exceed their 
targetÅfs NSR. The ÅgDefaultÅh NSR of an average sized human is 4, thus a Drifter would need to meet or 
exceed 4 on their D20 to hit.

	When a Vehicle is being piloted by a Drifter or an enemy, as long as they are moving, they will 
possess an MSR, Mechanized Survival Rating, based on the same size principles. If a Vehicle is not in 
motion and not moving, it is considered an object and can be hit with relative ease. Rigs & Titanic 
Vehicles have a 0 for their MSR, indicating that any attack against them will most likely hit - but with 
their armor and size, damaging them may be more complicated than hitting.

Armor Rating
	During their adventures, the Drifters will need to keep track of many things, but the Armor 
Rating of their Armor is important in combat. Armor Rating is how durable and protective the armor is, 
allowing the Drifter to shrug off certain attacks who can't be the threshold.
	NSR represents the Drifter's ability to avoid being shot or hit, Armor Rating allows some of those 
hits to bounce.

?
Combat Actions
	When it is the Drifter's turn they will have a number of Actions available to them equal to their 
current Combat Training, one to six. These Actions are split between Momentum and Reactive. 
Momentum Actions are when it is the Drifter's turn, allowing them to be more proactive in how they 
spend their Actions. Alternatively, a Reactive Action (or Reaction) is used when it is not the Drifter's 
Turn, allowing them to either defend themselves more actively, make snap decisions, or protect 
others.
	A Drifter may use as many or as Actions as they wish, but Momentum and Reactions use the 
same pool of Actions as well. If a Drifter uses all of their Actions during Momentum, they cannot use 
any in a Reaction, but if they are forced to use a number of Reactions, they may have nothing to do 
during their turn.
	Both Melee and Ranged Attacks do not have a traditional Skill like Bartering or Naturalism, 
instead any Drifter can reasonably use any weapon they get their hands on. However to become truly 
skilled in a Weapon, they will need a Weapon Proficiency, or a WP. A WP in a Weapon allows the Pilot to 
use Expertise on their attacks, modifying their attack with bonuses and penalties to inflict Called Shots, 
Feinting Attacks, or actually aiming properly.
	If a Drifter is unable (or unwilling) to use all of their Actions by the end of the Round, the Drifter 
converts all of their remaining Actions to their current Personal Initiative, allowing them to act earlier in 
the Action Order.

Momentum Actions
Attack, Melee
The Drifter makes an attempt to strike a Target 
who is adjacent to them on the field with a 
weapon or their fists. The Drifter makes a 
Combat Check of 1d20 + [Modifiers] versus 
TargetÅfs NSR. If successful, the Attack deals 
damage equal to their weapon. 

Attack, Ranged
The Drifter makes an attempt to strike a Target 
who is within range of their weapon. The Drifter 
makes a Combat Check of 1d20 + [Modifiers] 
versus TargetÅfs NSR. If successful, the Attack 
deals damage equal to their weapon. 

Delay
The Drifter holds their Action until a trigger occurs, 
allowing them to snap into Action once the trigger 
is set. For example: ÅgIf someone rounds the 
corner, I will shoot them with my gun.Åh

Maneuver
The Drifter is able to move up to their Movement 
Value dictated by their Reaction Derived 
Attribute.

Other
The Drifter performs an action that requires 
effort. For example: Opening a door requires no 
effort, kicking in the same door to break it open 
would take a [Other] Action. 

Power
The Drifter uses one of their Magic Spells or a 
Psychic Power - paying the MP / ESP Cost as well 
as resolving the effects. Different Magic Spells or 
Psychic Powers may require additional Actions to 
resolve. 

Refocus
The Drifter takes a second to breathe, soaking in 
the atmosphere of the battlefield around them. 
They increase their Initiative by +2 for the next 
Round or clear a Condition. 
Reload
The Drifter reloads a weapon on their person. If 
the Drifter does not have a Weapon Proficiency 
with the weapon, this takes two Actions. 

Skill
The Drifter uses one of their Skills. They will 
perform a Skill Check and determine the results.

Tool
The Drifter uses a tool, item, or object on their 
person or in the immediate area and resolves its 
effects.

Vehicle Combat Actions
	During Vehicle Combat, whoever is piloting the Vehicle may perform the same type of 
Actions as above, but instead relying on their Vehicles current options. In addition to those 
Momentum Actions, the Drifter has a number of Vehicle specific Actions. 

Vehicle System
The Drifter triggers one of their VehicleÅfs 
Upgrades, Traits, Items, or built-in safety 
features and resolves the effects immediately.

slam into an opposing vehicle or individual in an 
adjacent Space (or within 5 Meters). 
If it is against a different Vehicle that is currently 
not moving - both will take [5 - Ramming 
Size]D10 Damage to their Hull. If it is against a 
humanoid target with an NSR, they must make 
a Combat Check against double their NSR . 
Dealing [8 - Ramming Size]D10 Damage as 
either Standard or Mega Damage (Vehicle 
Dependent).
If the Vehicle has a Melee Weapon Hardpoint, 
they instead make an attack with their Melee 
Weapon first before registering the Ram. 
Ejection & Shutdown
The Drifter performs a Controlled Ejection, 
popping their cockpit to reveal themselves. For 
an additional Action, the Drifter may completely 
shutdown their Vehicle as well.

Emergency Repairs
The Drifter makes the appropriate Mechanics 
Skill Check to perform emergency repairs inside 
of their Vehicle. If they are successful, they add 
+1d6 Durability to their Hull.

Maneuver
The Drifter moves a number of Spaces equal to 
their VehicleÅfs Pace.

effort. For example: Moving debris to the side

Weapon Expertise
	Performing a Weapon Expertise requires that the Drifter has the appropriate Weapon 
Proficiency to enhance their attacks. The number of Actions required, in addition to the starting action 
to perform the attack, are noted in parentheses. Each Expertise may only be applied once to a single 
attack .

Aim Down Sights (Ranged) (+1)
The Drifter takes careful and precise aim right 
down their sights. They add +4 to their Combat 
Check. 

All-In-Strike (Melee) (+1)
The Drifter hefts their weapon and attempts to 
deliver a savage blow. They move up to their 
Combat Speed and attack the Target. If they 
are successful, it deals double (x2) damage. 

Called Strike (+1)
The Drifter attempts to strike a specific part of 
the body on their Target using a Single Shot or 
Melee Attack. Each Location has an Attack 
Penalty, but if successful, will strike the part.

Taking Damage
	Eventually the Drifter's luck will run out and they will be hit with a weapon that will deal damage 
to them. If the Drifter is a fool and they are hit with an Mega Damage Weapon, they die immediately 
(but may take a Scar) as they are vaporized, dismembered, or other horrible fates. If they are 
wearing armor or are hit with a Standard Damage Weapon, they will take damage as normal.
	When the Drifter takes damage, they will first reduce any Armor they are currently wearing 
first. A standard Gladiator Armor Set may have 60 Durability, allowing them to take up to 60 Mega 
Damage before it breaks open and reveals the guts of the Drifter. MD Armor does work on a 
threshold though, meaning that when MD Armor takes damage that would destroy it, the excess 
damage is lost as the Drifter staggers from the attack.
