Combat Mapping
	Combat takes place on the battlefield, forcing the Drifters to think accordingly to their 
surroundings to deal with the enemies before them (or attempt to run away faster than they can 
reach them). Battlefields are subdivided into two "types" of engagement distance: Field Combat and 
CQC. 

Field Combat	
	The most traditional type of battlefield that the Drifters will find themselves on is Field Combat. 
The GM will take a map and subdivide it into squares that represent 15 x 15 foot chunks of territory 
that the Drifters and their enemies may inhabit. 
	These squares are referred to as Spaces, pieces of ground that a Drifter can maneuver around 
in as well as dictate an engagement distance between enemies. The Drifters may attempt to cover 
ground equal to their Pace, effectively measuring how far a single Action may carry them.
	A Reaction  of 15 means that a Drifter has a Pace of 2 - this means that the Drifter may cover 2 
Spaces for one Action. If the Drifter had a 4 Reaction and a .5 Pace, they would take two Actions to 
move into an adjacent Space. 
 
	Due to the size of each of the Spaces, multiple Drifters or Enemies may be standing in a single 
Space unimpeded. If a Drifter and an Enemy are in the same Space, they are considered to be within 
Melee Range (Range 0). There is no strict limit to the number of people that may be in a single Space, 
though when a grenade is lobbed into it, most will attempt to scatter. 
	Each Space can only support one Vehicle of Mid-Size or Two Compacts. If a Vehicle were to 
enter a Space already occupied by another Vehicle, then a crash would occur, or worse. Personal size 
Vehicles are able to be with their rider regardless of the size, but these motorbikes and trikes can 
rarely take the firepower of a dedicated assailant. 
	Whenever a Drifter is using a Ranged Weapon, they will need to check the Range on the 
weapon itself. Any Weapon used inside of their Minimum Range or outside of their Maximum Range 
incurs a -2 Combat Check Penalty per Space. Certain Weapons, such as Melee, can only be used in 
certain situations or at certain ranges. 
	For example, using a Battle Rifle with a Maximum Range of 5, shooting at a Target at 7 Spaces 
would incur a -4 Combat Check Penalty on the Attacker.
 
	Certain Spaces may contain environmental features that may impact the ability for the Drifter 
to act or allow them additional options. These boil down to Cover, Free Fall, Rough, and Hazardous 
Terrain.
?

Cover
	Combat is a game of cat and mouse, and 
learning when to be which is often the key to 
success. Spaces with Cover have dedicated 
locations and areas to allow the Drifter to put 
something between them and their enemies. 
Cover comes in three varieties: Light, Heavy, and 
Complete.
	Light Cover covers situations of half-
concealment or obfuscation of attacks, as long as 
the Drifter is in a Space with Light Cover they may 
choose to gain a +4 to their NSR representing the 
increased difficulty to hit them. For an Action, the 
Drifter may attempt to further hide themselves or 
make themselves more difficult to hit, increasing 
the bonus to +6 to their NSR, but they may not 
Attack or make Reactions.
	Heavy Cover places hard walls, awkward 
angles, or encompassing foliage to mitigate 
attacks against the Drifter. As long as the cover 
can reasonably take up 80% of the Drifter's body, 
it's considered to be in Heavy Cover. While in 
Heavy Cover, they have a +6 to their NSR, but if 
they take an action to hunker down, this increases 
to a +10 to their NSR.
	Finally, Complete Cover has the Drifter 
break line of sight of the enemy entirely. No one 
can attack a target they can't reasonably see. If 
they are firing blindly at where the Drifter "should 
be" the Drifter has the hunkered down Heavy 
Cover bonus of +10 to their NSR as well as 
imposing a -10 penalty on the Attacker who 
cannot see them.
	If the Attacker is in the same Space as the 
Drifter, then Cover demotes by one step if the 
Attacker is using a Ranged Weapon. However, if 
the Attacker is declaring a Melee Attack, then 
cover does nothing as the assailant rushes their 
position immediately.
Rough Terrain
	Spaces with Rough Terrain are difficult to 
navigate due to sludge, foliage, water, or anything 
that would hinder movement. The Drifter's Pace is 
considered to be two steps lower than it actually 
is when attempting to leave the Space.
	For example, if a Drifter is knee deep in a 
swamp, their Pace of 3 would go down to 1. While 
a Drifter at 1 would go down to .25 instead. A 
Drifter cannot fall below .25 Pace.

Hazardous Terrain
	The Space is actively attempting to harm 
or at least damage the Drifter outright. These 
Spaces come in three varieties: Standard 
Hazards, Mega Hazard, and Giga Hazards each 
correlating to the 2d6 Damage that will incur as 
long as the Drifter is in the Space or walks through 
the Space to reach a different location.

Standard
Mega
Giga
Fire, Poison Gas
Plasma, Magic
Lava, Nuclear Waste

Free Fall
	Reasonably speaking, this could be 
referred to as "Flight." If a Drifter has the ability to 
fly through equipment, abilities, or features they 
may loom above the Space itself being treated as 
if they were +1 Space away, but ignoring all 
Features. But they may still declare a Melee 
Attack in the Space below them, swooping down 
to deliver a blow. If an enemy also has flight, the 
two Engaged targets treat the "Free Fall Zone" as 
if they were in their own Space.
	The Free Fall aspect comes from the more 
likely scenario of falling. Every "Space" above the 
current one incurs a stacking 3d6 Damage to the 
Drifter should they fall from it. Thus falling 30 Feet 
(2 Spaces) would deal 6d6 Damage. However, 
this Damage is either SD if the Target does not 
have Armor on, or MD if they do. This SD Damage 
targets the DrifterÅfs Health directly instead of 
resolving Endurance first.
	Armor may cushion one's blow, but parts 
will be jumbled, containment protocols punctured, 
and disaster looming.

?
CQC 
	Most firefights that occur are rarely the practiced military engagements or structured battles in 
the field. Someone draws a knife in a bar, another quickly draws a revolver with enough force to 
punch through armor, while the Psychic readies to cut both down in a second. 
	CQC, or Close Quarters Combat, are situations in which the current fight is not occuring at a 
reasonable distance to represent via Field Combat. Normally, these are spur of the moment combats 
where everyone is within 15 to 30 Feet of one another. Rather than tracking exact distances, the entire 
area becomes awash in combat as both sides either open up or charge one another.
	CQC Battles are considered to be "Theatre of the Mind" in which most enemies are within 
reasonable distance to pop off snap shots or get into melee at a moment's notice. Treat all CQC 
Battles as if they are taking place in the same Space for purposes of Weapon Ranges and abilities. 
	Should the battle evolve beyond the natural limits of the CQC, then Field Combat may be 
elected to be used to represent the expanding battlefield unfolding. But few tend to last that long.

Vehicles on the Map
	Similar to Drifter on Drifter battles, Vehicles can find themselves playing a massive part in 
different fights. The basic rules still apply to both scenarios - Vehicles in Field Combat will take up a 
number of Spaces in the field, representing their "girth" as much as their use. A Large or Mid-Size 
Vehicle can take up one Space and still support an entire party defending it from attackers. Rigs 
take up to six Spaces depending on their load and cargo, while a Titanic Vehicle outright replaces 
up to 16 (4 x 4) Spaces depending on the size.
	If the Vehicle has a Turret or otherwise can be used for combat, the Vagabond must be in the 
Vehicle (taking a Momentum Action to enter if they are outside) to use the equipment successfully. 
However, as long as a Vehicle is in a Space, the Drifters may choose to use it as Cover.

Magic Power
	Magic Power, or MP, is an abstraction created by accredited universities to explain the 
phenomenon of Magicians Ågrunning out of energyÅh during prolonged use of magical power. The 
explanations for why this occurs vary from internal chemistry, intangible forces, to the more 
reasonable ÅgMagic Power is created by others to oppress less capable magicians.Åh Regardless of the 
truth, when the Drifter uses magical powers they are drawing from their total MP to project it 
outward. If they were to ever run out, they would be able to manage little more than a few measly 
sparks and pull a muscle.

Magic Power (MP)
[WIL x 2] + [Background / Occupation Bonus / CL]

	Whenever the Magician uses a Spell, they will calculate the total Strain it costs their body to 
use, reducing their Magic Power when itÅfs cast. A Spell Strain is equal to the amount of components it 
takes to cast it successfully - trained Magicians have developed methods to reduce the amount of 
Strain individual magical abilities cost, but it mostly depends on the Schools of Thought that dominate 
the method in which magic is taught to others.?

	Magic Power recovers to full after a complete rest 
(8 Hours for Humans), ingesting Prana Potions, or by 
soaking in the latent energy of Earthblood. 
	In desperate circumstances, each of the Schools of 
Thought have devised their own methods to recover 
Magic Power, the ÅgQuick and DirtyÅh method. Often this 
requires the Magician to perform some variety of action or 
sacrifice something in exchange for a few drops of Magic 
Power they can squeeze from their bodies. 
 
	Standing by or hunting for Earthblood Geysers are a 
sure way for the Magician to recover their Magic Power 
quickly. Soaking in the latent energy to replenish their own 
stockpile. Standing by a Geyser or Wound for too long will 
invoke a Power Surge as the energy starts supercharging 
the Magician's body. This causes them to undergo mood 
swings, vast quantities of Magic Power and manic 
restlessness.
	Many who experience the rush feel dead inside 
when the Wound closes or they are taken away from the 
Geyser directly. Often coming down off of it hard by 
resting for multiple days in a row.

Heat & Burnout
	Magic is not without its risks, often frequent and deadly for those who donÅft know how to 
control their newfound power. Whenever a Magician is using Magic, they generate Heat. Heat 
measures a mixture of their internal body temperature as well as the latent aura around them as they 
start casting. Normally, this will dissipate as soon as the spell ends, but there are some considerations. 

Total Heat
[WIL + Ranks in Magical Occupations] + [Modifiers]

	Whenever a Magician casts magic, they will be generating Strain that will reduce their Magic 
Points. If this Strain is higher than their Total Heat, the Spell fizzles, being simply too powerful for the 
Magician to use successfully. This occurs more among young Magi training their first few techniques. 
However, if a Magician is choosing to Sustain a Spell, they will treat the Total Strain as being their 
current Heat. The more spells the Magician has working at once the more their body is heating up and 
failing to cast more complicated spells. 
	So what is a Burnout?
	Burning Out is the term used to describe Magicians who have expended far more power than 
they naturally are able to, burning their natural Magic Power away to cast spells they normally canÅft. A 
Magician of CL 5 or higher may cast spells over their Total Heat if they make up the difference by 
reducing their Maximum Magic Power  to continue using their magic freely. Reducing their Magic 
Power to 0 this way causes the Magician to completely Burn Out, losing their Magic Power entirely as 
well as their ability to Cast - though they may now take up the Burnout Magic Occupation. 

?
Grimoire
	The MagicianÅfs Grimoire is the collection of all of their Magical Abilities they have amassed over 
their lifetime. Each of these books, objects, or cryptic writings contain the Magicians Spells, Gestures, 
and Glyphs that allow them to filter their magic power through reliably.
	Spells are the foundational aspect of all Magic, the ability to shape oneÅfs Magic Power into 
something tangible. Each Spell is broken down into separate categories representing its nature  as 
well as what Gestures and Glyphs are available. If a Magician does not know a Spell, they cannot 
shape their Magic Power into anything - often seen by a Magician flailing haphazardly for something 
to happen under bad incantations or ritualized abilities.
	If the Spell would be able to do Damage, the Magician may choose it to be either MD or SD. In 
addition, if the Spell has (Defined) next to it, the Spell must dictate what it is doing: Summon Weapon 
(Revolver) is a different Spell than Summon Weapon (Sword)

Å@Å@Å@Gestures allow for a degree of precision in regards to Magic Power. It represents the second 
layer of a Spell, focusing it down or empowering it in different ways to enable the Magician to get 
more out of it. These are also loud and noticeable forcing the Magician to perform movements, 
incantations, or other effects to draw out the necessary changes to the Spell itself. Only one Gesture 
may be applied to a Spell itself, but they may either Consuming (only being able to be applied once) 
or Repeating (able to be applied up to three times). 
Å@Å@Å@Gestures can technically be applied to any Spell, but for purposes of Errant Earth, they are 
restricted to what is being stated here.

Å@Å@Å@Each Magical Ability used by a Magician is a [Spell], augmented by a [Gesture] and a [Glyph] to 
heighten its effects. However, the Magician is restricted to what Spells, Gestures, and Glyphs they 
possess as they are all written in their Grimoire.
Å@Å@Å@The GrimoireÅfs Size indicates how many of each type they may have access to. Multiple 
Grimoires may contain different abilities for each, allowing for creative Magicians to ÅgdrawÅh the right 
Grimoire at the right time - or at least hunt them down to add to their own growing collection. Once a 
Grimoire is full, they can no longer sustain any additional Spells, Gestures, or Glyphs.
This leads to Inscribing & Rote Magic.
	Inscribing Magic is the act of purposefully embedding the Spell, Gesture, or Glyph onto the 
soul of the Magician, turning themselves into a living Grimoire of sorts. When one of these are 
Inscribed, they become a permanent fixture of the Magician's repertoire, able to be drawn out 
regardless of whether or not they have their Grimoire. However, each Magician may only sustain a 
total of [1 + CL/5] Inscriptions at once, meaning that a CL 15 Magician would have access to 
Inscribing four Spells, Gestures, or Glyphs on their person .
Å@Å@Å@Rote Magic has been trained to near perfection by the Magician. Every 3 CL a Magician may 
elect to create a Rote Magic Spell - taking any Spell, Gesture, and Glyph they have available in their 
Grimoire and reducing the Strain Cost by half as long as it is cast the exact same way with no 
alterations to the nature of the Spell. Rote Spells are ÅgLockedÅh for the Magician, but are simple for 
them to cast to let them do so with far less stress on their body. 
 
	The final important note about Grimoires and the construction of magical powers before the 
descriptions of each is the act of Countering Magic. If the Drifter has a Grimoire or has Internalized 
over half of the components of a Spell, then they may attempt to Counter the Spell as a Reaction. The 
Drifter makes an Opposed WIL Attribute Check against the caster. If the Drifter defeats the Caster, 
then they will expend an equal amount of Magic Power to disrupt the casting and cancel it out (still 
forcing the original expenditure). If they fail, they are not fast enough to stop it, but they do not spend 
MP on the Counter attempt.
	Counterspelling is seen as a massive insult to almost every Magician, though the only way that 
someone would know what Spells are being cast would be to continue casting the same magic over 
and over again, or if someone were to have stolen their Grimoire . . .


The Wayward Notes - Identifying Magic
Identifying Magic is not a difficult feat unto itself, whether just detecting traces of Glimmer or perceiving the 
distortion of reality with their own eyes. Identifying the types of Magic being used is more difficult. When a 
Magical Power is cast in the presence of a Magician or someone trained in detecting Magic - they may make a 
Check to see what the Spell is using either their School of Thought Skill or Comprehension Attribute.
The chart below is assuming that the Spell is being used ÅgIn-CombatÅh and moments are all the Drifter has to 
recognize it. If the Drifter is studying someone while relaxed, they all do this with a +20% to their Skill Check, but 
no change for having No Formal Training.

Inland Empire
	The mind is a primal soup in which nothing emerges 
without a hundred thousand filters self-imposed by the 
constraints of the physical body and false ego. The psionic 
dream is to free the mind from the burden of flesh and 
decouple the self from it, an awakened entity that may 
cross the veil.
	A Psychic is an individual blessed, or perhaps cursed, 
with their ability to manipulate their Extra Sensory Power 
to manifest their various psychic abilities - empowering 
themselves, manipulating others, or radiating power 
outward to grant them any edge they can muster.
	When the Drifter increases their Character Level or 
someone attempts an Awakening Ritual on them, they will 
roll 1d100 under their Psychic Potential. If they succeed, they 
open their Psychic Eye and gain their base amount of ESP 
in addition to any bonuses granted to them by their 
Background or Occupation.

 Extra Sensory Power
	Extra Sensory Power, or ESP, is an abstraction of the mental strength and ego of a Psychic. The 
more one tries to manipulate the mind and the world around them, the more they twist and curl from 
the inside out. When a Drifter is using their Psychic Powers, they are drawing directly from their ESP to 
resolve the effect. When their ESP is reaching critical levels, the PsychicÅfs mind begins warping and 
tiring out, their body giving up to keep them going. 

Extra Sensory Power (ESP)
[ANM x 2] + [Background / Occupation Bonus / CL]

Å@Å@Å@Whenever the Psychic uses one of their Powers, they will calculate their total Strain to their 
body to use, rending their ESP when itÅfs used. While the Psychic Strain is reliable, it also forces the 
Psychic to constantly push themselves further and further to match their rivals - placing more Strain 
on their already fragile psyche.


	Extra Sensory Power recovers to full after a 
complete rest (8 Hours for Humans). Other methods 
include meditation, rampant drug abuse, or simply 
consuming the Psychic Potential of others.
	Devouring is the process where a Psychic absorbs 
the latent energy of a defeated psychic entity or other 
Psychic. Completely recharging (100% Recovery) 
themselves at the cost of the rather morbid interpretation 
by most. Other methods are more debatable, such as 
keeping living batteries, relying on empaths, or simply 
getting juiced to ward off the voices. 
 
	Psychics donÅft sleep traditionally though, when they 
do ÅgsleepÅh they enter their personal Inland Empire - a 
reflection of their inner psyche. Most are content with 
staying on the edge in the quasi-dreamlike state, others 
venture deeper into their Imperial Domain and retain more 
conscious thought and actions. Though time will slow down 
in this place as they are free to reconstruct their memories, 
talk to their ego forms, or simply meditate easier.

Heat & Pushing
	Psychic Powers rely on the strength of the user just as much as it does on their willingness to not 
use their powers. Whenever a Psychic is using any of their Psychic Abilities, they generate Heat. Heat is 
the measure of the Psychic's brain physically heating up to compensate for the increased stress of 
their abilities. Normally, Psychics "Vent" their Heat as soon as it's generated, resulting in a thin aura 
around them that mimics their current Glimmer.

Total Heat
[ANM + Ranks in Psychic Occupations] + [Modifiers]

	Whenever a Psychic is using their abilities, they will be generating Strain that will reduce their 
ESP. If this Strain is higher than their Total Heat, their ability flickers and eventually fades without 
accomplishing much due to their natural safety measures preventing them from doing so. If a Psychic 
chooses to Sustain a Power, they will instead treat that Total Strain as being their current Heat. The 
more abilities than the Psychic is maintaining at once, the more their mind and body have to keep up, 
struggling to use even the most basic abilities.
	So how does a Psychic push past their natural limits?
	One of the first steps of being a Psychic is learning the push-and-pull of the energy that lies 
dormant inside of them. Any Psychic at CL 5 or higher may decide to Push their Psychic Abilities to 
their limit, being able to manifest or sustain abilities past their Total Heat - in exchange the Psychic 
must begin hemorrhaging their ESP equal to double the excess Heat . They may choose to Sustain 
any abilities over their Maximum Heat, paying triple the ESP over their Heat Limit at the end of every 
Round or 30 Seconds of real time. 

The Wayward Notes - Boiling Point for Psycho-Magicians 
	Heat is used by both Psychics and Magicians, drawing upon the same principles explained in 
different ways. In the rare moments that a Psychic Magician is born, they will need to share their 
new Heat pool together. 
If a Drifter is both a Psychic and a Magician, their new formula for Heat is [(WIL+ANM)/2+[Ranks in 
Magician Occupations] + [Ranks in Psychic Occupations] + Modifiers. Luckily they are able to support 
more heat overtime, but only those trained in the arts of both can hope to use their MP and ESP 
together. 
?
Mesial Powers
	Deep within the Mesial Void of the Mind does the Inland Emperor sit upon its throne - the 
source of all of the Psychic's power begins and ends with the Inland Emperor and their whims.
	Mesial Powers are the passive effects that a Psychic is naturally born with and develop 
independently of any dedicated skill that the Drifter is partaking in. There are only three Mesial 
Powers, being common enough that all Psychics are assumed to have them in some capacity, sowing 
some distrust when appropriate. 
The Chorus (CL 1)
	When a Psychic is first awoken, the first 
thing they hear are their thoughts, the next is 
someone close to them and their thoughts. 
Psychics naturally can hear the surface thoughts 
of those around them, more concerned about the 
immediate moments in front of them or the 
lingering doubts that seem to haunt them. In 
densely packed urban environments, a thousand 
cacophonous voices are telling simultaneously 
directly into the mind of the Psychic at all times. 
	It takes years of training to fully shut out 
the voices, though it does become background 
noise after some time. 
	A Psychic may choose to focus on a 
particular person if the group is ten or less, the 
target does not have a Cybernetic Stress of 5+, is 
not a robot, is not a magician, or possess Psychic 
Resistance. If they do such, their inner voice is 
more clear and can be heard - this is how many 
psychic communities tend to talk with one 
another rather than verbal sparring. 

Telepathic (CL 3)
	The PsychicÅfs Chorus has matured to the 
point that it allows them to communicate with 
other Psychics silently through telepathy at a 
distance of roughly 30 Feet. 
	At CL 5, the PsychicÅfs Range increases to 
60 Feet and they may ÅgLinkÅh with others via the 
Trojan Horse to speak to them with Telepathy 
even if they are not Psychics.
The Trojan Horse (CL 5)
	If a Psychic were to place their bare skin 
against another individual, their mind opens up 
before them. During this brief trance  state, the 
Psychic is free to wander the mind of their victim, 
their personal Inland Fiefdom, as long as they 
stay connected.
	If the Psychic attempts this on someone 
with Psychic Resistance, they must make an 
opposed ANM vs WIL Save to "break into" the 
entity's mind. If this is done with another Psychic, 
feedback occurs and both feel a shock through 
their system. Some find this extremely stimulating 
in all of the wrong ways. 

Murmurs (CL 10)
	As the Psychic grows in strength, so does 
the Murmering. The Inland Emperor tends to 
make their voice known at inopportune times or 
at critical junctures, act less like a moral guide 
and more as an accelerant to any action done by 
the Psychic.
	By the time the Murmering begins in 
honesty, is it often too late. The Inland Emperor's 
voice can be heard when they sleep, when they 
close their eyes, and any moment they are not 
perfectly diligent they will often end up in a 
dialogue with their inner self demanding action, 
sustenance, or other ego-driven things. 
	Some embrace it. Some reject it. Others 
hang themselves after it gets too loud.

Resonant Powers
	A Psychic's Resonant Powers are built from a set of different foundations, each relating to how 
the Psychic chooses to approach situations and seek a harmonious discord with them in some way.
	Depending on the Background and Occupation of the Drifter, they will begin with a number of 
Resonant Powers they will open up as they would any other Skill. Each Resonant Power is, for all intents 
and purposes, a Skill that the Drifter may use, performing regular Skill Checks to determine the quality 
of the power itself.

	Resonant Powers obey the same limitations as Skill Checks with a consistent growth rate until 
they reach 100% in which they will drop to 0% Development. The Drifter will need to either manually 
improve their Powers through training or rely on the teachings of masters to impart their wisdom for a 
price.
	Whenever a Resonant Power is used against someone, they may have a chance to resist it with 
a WIL Save. Whenever the Psychic is using their Resonant Power against someone who is aware of 
them using their Psychic Powers, an Awakened Psychic, Awakened Magician, or has latent Magical or 
Psychic Resistance may attempt a save automatically. If someone is not capable of any of those, then 
they have no manual defense against the power being used against them and may not even realize it 
was used against them.

Charge Powers
	When people traditionally think about Psychic, they either drift toward the abuse of their 
Resonant Powers or awe-inspiring strength of their Charge Powers. Charge Powers are the most 
direct application of the Psychic's ability to manifest their ESP. Whether they are using their power to 
directly harm others or protect themselves, the distortion of space and twinkle in the aether is enough 
to know that one is being used.
	Rather than straining their mind as with Resonant Powers, Charge Powers rely on the Psychic 
pushing out and expelling a set amount of their ESP to accomplish a preset goal. The appearance and 
nature of these powers are variable, but will inevitably alert any other Psychic to what's going on. Of 
course, Psychics are tricky when they need to be. When the field is even, every gambit has its place. 
 
	When a Psychic acquires a Charge Power they will open it up at its base level, or First Order. As 
the Psychic develops in power and begins to hone their abilities further, the Psychic may take 
additional Charge Powers or increase the Order of their Charge Powers by adding additional tricks, 
quirks, or empowering them directly. Each Psychic may only reach the Sixth Order in any of their 
Charge Powers, adding any more causing too much mental stress to manifest properly. Each Order 
will increase the base ESP Cost of the Charge Power, a Psychic may be able to Ågturn offÅh different 
Orders, but it will close off all abilities Ågabove itÅh as well . 
	If the Psychic wishes to "reset" themselves - they will need to undergo a complete mind cleanse, 
slipping into a 1d6 Day Coma as their mind mentally restructures itself. This allows the Psychic to 
redistribute any of their Orders among any of their Charge Powers. Each time this is done, add an 
additional +1d6 Days to their Coma as their mind slips deeper into the Mesial Void.

Latent Powers
	Deep within every Psychic lies their Inland Empire, a bastion of who they are on a physical, 
metaphysical, and transcendental basis. With their powers emanating from the Mesial Void and their 
Inland Emperor, it's no surprise there are one-of-a-kind powers that manifest.
	Latent Powers bubble up from the Mesial Void, demonstrating a power tied fundamentally to 
the abilities of the Psychic.  Whenever the Psychic reaches a point in Power, the Psychic will gain a 
unique Skill Tag called [Latent].
	When the [Latent] Skill Tag is added to a Skill, the Psychic has developed Psychic Powers 
relating to that Skill. By all intents and purposes, the Skill is now considered a Psychic Skill for purposes 
of advancement or abilities. This manifests as the Skill growing increasingly psychic dependent and 
allowing for supernatural phenomenon to manifest.
	To determine the base cost of their new Psychic Power, consult this chart.

Adventure on Errant Earth
	The Errant Earth is filled with a number of terrible hazards and diabolical plans that the Drifters 
will inevitably fall into. During their adventure, the Drifters will be getting into gun fights and debates 
simply enough, but more adventurous Drifters may find themselves far outside the comforts of 
civilization or at the heart of its rotting inside.

Travel
	When the Drifters are attempting to reach a location farther than a quick jaunt away, they'll be 
travelling. With the breakdown of infrastructure in America and beyond, the people of the Errant Earth 
have taken to carving their own roads out of the world toward major settlements and resources.
	Not to imply that connection is widespread, a road today is a bandit toll booth the next. Roads 
are for those who have the privilege to protect them, to keep them "safe enough" from the 
roughriders or enemies in the woods. For now at least.
 
	Whenever the Drifters are going to travel to a new location, they will need to choose how they 
are going to get there, how long it'll take, packing enough supplies, and then ride into the sunset, or 
perhaps walk slowly with fifty-pounds of supplies on their back.
	When the Drifters know where they want to go they'll first need to determine the distance 
between the two points. This is measured in American Miles, or the Mile. After determining the 
location, the Drifters will need to choose how they are going to reach their destination. This is done by 
choosing the Road, Path, Hazard, or Wayfinding. 
	Roads are reliable and are maintained by the local governments in the area. The Great Lakes 
Confederacy has a road going from Stony Point to Chigeon, Buffalo Falls, and Bay Town with Chigeon 
having another road riding through Milwaukee and Green Bay. However, with the conflict hitting a 
boiling point the roads are also a reliable place to find some suckers and be spotted before the 
Drifters know they are being looked at. 
	Paths are the unofficial roads, the backways that towns and isolated homesteads use to mark 
the way. Being in the "know" is half the battle when finding paths and cutting a deal with a local for the 
"secret path" may be ideal. Or lead into disaster in the middle of nowhere. 
	Finally there are Hazardous Areas and Wayfinding. Hazard Areas are pock marked in 
extreme danger or in the midst of a cataclysmic event. It's difficult to navigate without proper 
assistance and even more impressive to get out with their limbs attached. Though Wayfinding is 
arguably the most dangerous, striking off into the great unknown may be able to hide their trail and 
not alert any suspecting enemies, but being in the middle of nowhere with nothing but a navigator's 
keen eye and memory is something few wish to experience. 
?

the wise tend to find their burial markers. Travel Challenges are small

if they had a Travel Challenge or Encounter that day. If the result has two of 
the same number, or ÅgDubs,Åh they have a Random Encounter in addition to 
their Travel Challenge.

The Wayward Notes - ATB vs Skill Travel Challenges
	Rolling for a random Travel Challenge has the GM determine if it is an ATB or Skill Challenge. 
ATB Travel Challenges are brute forcing the situation as hard as possible, with 8 Attributes it's also 
easy to roll a 1d8 to determine the relevant Attribute to be tested in that situation. Skill Challenges 
are a bit more haphazard, due to the breadth of available Skills for the Drifters to rely on. 
	When a Skill Travel Challenge occurs, the GM will need to have a rough idea what the 
situation is and how to bypass it. The safest option is relying on Wilderness Skills to carry the day, 
though the GM may always roll on the following chart to determine what the scenario is to present 
to the Drifters.

Demeanor
	No one is an island, the Drifter will encounter a number of people on their adventures, from 
close allies, scheming tyrants, and the occasional bystander willing to help or talk it out. The Drifter will 
be naturally measuring their relationship with people and situations through their Demeanor.
	Demeanor is the measure of how receptive others are toward the Drifter and what they have 
to say to them. Each Drifter is different and the initial impressions some leave can have a lasting 
impact on people's perception of them. Not to say everyone is going to be immediately friendly 
towards a Drifter with good looks and smooth voice, though it does help.
	Base Demeanor shows how receptive a person is toward the Drifter. A Demeanor of 10 to 12 
may indicate being neutral to a bit friendly, while a Demeanor of 19 may indicate obsession with the 
Character to the point of being unhealthy. But, having a Demeanor of 4 with someone may indicate a 
simmering hatred that can't be quelled easily. 

Influence Checks
	What does Demeanor do though? Demeanor grants a Modifier for the Drifter when using their 
Attributes or Skills to manipulate, persuade, or convince someone to do something. This is called an 
Influence Check.
	Influence Checks have the Drifter make a Attribute or Skill Check against the target in an effort 
to convince them to do something. The more absurd or outlandish the request, the more difficult it 
becomes.

	Influencing using Attributes is trying to overwhelm the opponent through sheer force of 
character or actions, prompting the target to make a Willpower Save to oppose it. However, the limits 
of these Influence Checks are simple and direct - "I want to get into the bar" is a simple enough 
request and a charismatic person may be able to bat their eyelashes and walk in unimpeded. 
Alternatively, using a Skill Check is more focused and allows the Drifter to make more nuanced and 
complicated requests, using a combination of smooth talkings, schmoozing, and presentation to get 
the results needed. "I want to get into the bar while hiding a holdout pistol in my belt" would prompt 
the Drifter to make the proper Skill Check to navigate out of this situation. If a Skill Check succeeds, 
often there iss no need to make a Willpower Save unless it is something extremely suspicious or 
dangerous.





Changing Demeanor
Å@Å@Å@Demeanor shifts and changes the more someone interacts with another person. Most of the 
time the various characters and creatures being influenced are in the background and may only come 
up again later, but others may be Side Characters in their own right.
	The Drifter may write down a number of Contacts as specified in their Demeanor and actively 
shape their perception of the Drifter and their issues. Some of these "slots" may be filled in before the 
Drifter even begins their adventure, others may be written in as the Drifter wanders.
	If the Drifter  works with, assists, or actively helps a Contact they will increase their Demeanor 
by +1 at the end of the Session. This indicates that they have become more receptive and friendly with 
the Character, working together to help one another. On the other hand, if the Character is asking 
huge favors or making intimidating demands, their Demeanor may lower by -1 / -2 / -4 depending on 
the severity. 
	It's far harder to build a relationship than it is to destroy one.

Being Influenced
	The Drifter isn't the only one with the ability to influence others, any Character with the 
appropriate skills and abilities may also attempt to influence the Drifter to perform actions or compel 
them into a situation.
	The Drifter being ÅginfluencedÅh by others is an easy way to develop the Contact. Taking time off 
to go work a side gig, a dangerous request, or running simple errands may go a long way for them.
	However, if the Drifter wants to resist this Influence they will be making a Willpower Save with a 
penalty equal to the Demeanor of the requestor. Should they fail they'll be forced to go along with the 
request or suffer catastrophic Demeanor loss . Success means they ward off helping them (for now) 
though it won't improve their relationship at all.

Horror Factor
Å@Å@Å@The world is filled with terrifying things, brain eating slugs, face melting hazards, horrible brain 
frying psychics, and the occasional dimensional freak of nature that vibrates in and out of our reality. 
Situations and individuals may have a Horror Factor to measure how horrible and frightening 
something is.
	Horror Factor is measured from 0 to a negative value. Most entities in the world do not have a 
Horror Factor, even possessing a 0 instills a certain uneasiness in others. When the Drifters encounter 
someone with a Horror Factor, they will make an Anima or Willpower Save and apply their Horror 
Factor as a penalty to their Check.
	Anima based Horror Factor is physical and immediate, a revulsion that causes others to recoil in 
fear. Willpower based Horror Factor is emotional or cerebral, relying more on the implication of "What 
if" than anything immediate. In short, Anima is used for watching a friend be vaporized by a creature, 
Willpower for realizing the creature is terrifying to begin with.
	Succeeding at a Horror Factor Save has the Drifter harden their resolve, nothing occurs and 
they take no immediate penalty to the situation. If they are confronted with a different variant of the 
Horror Factor (Anima or Willpower) they will need to make the Save again. Failing the Horror Factor 
Save has the Drifter flinch, taking a penalty to all actions equal to the Horror Factor for the remainder 
of the scene or until the creature is defeated.
	If Horror Factor is 0, then no penalties are given, but the revulsion and recoil is immediately felt 
and may be acted upon by an opposing force.

Companions & Mounts
	During their travels, the Drifters may encounter others who are willing to help them and even 
tag along to offer their skills and talents. Companions are the catch-all term for those brave souls 
willing to accompany the Drifters into the thick of things.
	The requisite for being a Companion is "Free Will" which is the ability for them to reject the 
Drifters or simply run away when they get scared enough.
	Companions have one to three Concepts which measure their relevant abilities and skills in a 
condensed fashion. A Companion may be a "Coalition Soldier 15" meaning that whenever a Check is 
called in which it is relevant, they will use their [Coalition Soldier] Concept as either their Attribute or 
Skill (multiplying their Concept by 5).
	Each Companion will have Endurance equal to their highest Concept and Health equal to half 
of that in addition to any armor and weapons they may carry. Finally, each Companion will have 
Loyalty measured from 0 to 20. Whenever the Companion is ordered to do something dangerous, 
risky, or outside of their expertise, they will make a Loyalty Check by rolling a D20 under their Loyalty. 
	If it is successful, the Companion will attempt the task or at least provide what assistance they 
can.  If they fail this Check, if their Loyalty is above 0, they will lose 1d6 Loyalty and may refuse the 
request outright. If they had 0 or would reduce them to 0, they will leave the group at their earliest 
convenience.
	A unique type of companion is a Mount, rather than being a thinking person with a life to live 
and problems to worry about, mounts are animals that are ridden by the Drifter for various reasons. 
Each Mount will either be a Quick, Draft, or Caravan Mount, with their first Concept being labelled as 
such. 
	Controlling a Mount requires the use of the Animal Husbandry Skill to manage them in the midst 
of the action. The Mount is by itself intelligent enough to be given orders that they'll follow, Loyalty only 
being tested when presented with something that could frighten, excite, or injure them. 

The Wayward Notes - Mounts in Combat
	If the Drifter is riding their majestic horse, lizardbat, or raptorhawk into battle, theyÅfll need to 
make sure what theyÅfre doing.

Exposure
Å@Å@Å@Oftentimes the real killer of vagabonds and strangers on the Errant Earth is a combination of 
the elements or other haphazard situations. Exposure is the catch-all term for various environmental 
hazards that the Drifters may encounter.
	When in a situation that would constitute Exposure, such as being in the blazing heat or biting 
cold, the GM will establish the Exposure Rating starting at D4. Every Scene in which the Drifters are 
present and subjected to the Exposure they will reduce their Endurance by the die size indicated. Thus 
a D10 Heat Exposure would reduce everyone's Endurance by D10 every Scene they are in without the 
proper gear to protect them.
Å@Å@Å@Exposure may be declared as either a Stacking or Consistent modifier. A Stacking Modifier 
increases the die size by one step every Scene the Drifter is exposed to, raising gradually until they die 
or are lost. While a Consistent modifier will remain at its Exposure Rating until a change in conditions or 
a situation has occurred. 
	Hazardous Environment Suit Armor has a Resistance Rating for different types of exposure, 
lowering the die size by a number of steps equal to the Resistance Rating. A full Coalition Self-
Contained Armor System has a Resistance of 5 toward Heat, Cold, and Radiation. Thus if they were 
subjected to a D20 level of Heat, normally lethal to anyone else, they would instead reduce it to D4.

Downtime Actions
	The Drifters are always on the move and often only staying in one place long enough to rest up 
before roving out once again. However, during these moments of contemplation and peace, they 
have some downtime to pursue their own objectives and goals. 
	During Downtime, the Drifters are allowed to converse, relax, or work on various projects they 
have before them. The Drifters are free to pursue their own goals during Downtime, with the GM 
electing to resolve Scenes involving the Drifters in any order they wish or on a first come, first serve, 
basis. 
Dramatis Personae
The Drifter begins a conversation with an important 
member of the ensemble or others that may be a part of 
their immediate group. If they are in a settlement, they are 
free to talk with anyone in it.  

Field Repairs
The Drifter patches up their vehicles or armor themselves. 
They make the appropriate Skill Check to improve 
Durability efficiently, or increase Durability by +1d6.
If there is a workshop or other self-repair centers, they 
may increase this bonus to +1d12. 

Private
The Drifter goes off to resolve their own private issues, 
others may tag along if they wish. 

Resting 
The Drifter rests and relaxes, recovering their Endurance 
or Health naturally. If they do not need to recover, they 
may instead relax socially with others attempting to 
recover, increasing their Recovery by +2.

Stocking Up
The Drifter hits the markets or starts a scavenging spree in 
the local area. They may find something useful, or lose 
what little credits they have.

The Marketplace
	In the ruins of the Old World, the belief that one manÅfs trash is anotherÅfs treasure has taken on 
different meanings and nuances. Filled with old technology and mixed with the bustling industrial hubs 
of the new world, the Errant Earth has a plethora of weapons, armor, gear, and nearly anything else 
that a Drifter may need to succeed at their adventures and survive to tell others about their deeds.
	But where there is a need, there is the siren call of profit. Nothing is ever truly free on the Errant 
Earth, whether it must be paid in credit, deed, or blood is to be seen. 

The Wayward Notes - Credits, Baubles, and You
	Throughout the Marketplace, the term ÅgCreditsÅh will be mentioned frequently. Great Lakes 
Credits, or GLC, are the default currency in the Great Lakes Confederacy and most of the 
surrounding area. If the GM is not setting the game in the Confederacy, then the term ÅgCreditsÅh 
may be changed to anything from Marks, Sticks, Bells, Dollars, or any other kind of legal tender. The 
costs presented in Errant Earth are assumed to be a Partially Industrialized Post-Apocalypse 
Society.
	If the GM wishes to adjust the prices for different regions, situations, or currency deviations, 
then modifying costs in 25% increments is reasonable. If something is 100 in a ÅgStandardÅh area, an 
isolated community may have it cost 300 (300%) or a much more wealthy area with more ready 
access to the good may have it cost 50 (-50%).

Weapons
	The cruel reality of the modern day is that people get hurt, often by other people, but the occasional raging monsters or invasions 
of troglodyte Exos tend to leave many dead. Since the dawn of man, the weapon has served as a symbol of defiance against this reality 
and has reinforced it all the more. Over the millenia and across the stars, weapon development has never ceased and the desire to get 
an ÅgedgeÅh on the opposition via superior firepower has defined entire eras and civilization. 
	On the Errant Earth, weaponry is a symbol of the old and new world, the rifle holding back the horde of creatures in this hostile 
world just as much as being the tool used to place others in the dirt. Weapon innovation has only been matched by the constantly 
expanding needs and tastes of the world, building more elaborate weapons or putting more firepower per bullet. 
	ItÅfs theoretically impossible to categorize every variant of every weapon on the Errant Earth, a single rifle may have a dozen 
variations in a region alone let alone the countless variants and half-variants made by competition or rivals in others. To symbolize the 
most basic weapons in the field, they are referred to as ÅgDefaultÅh Weapons, while the name may change, the ÅgDefaultÅh Weapon is the 
standard template in which all its variants and mimics are built from .
 
	A WeaponÅfs Damage is the number of Damage Die that the Drifter will roll on a 
successful attack, reducing the Durability of their Armor or dealing Endurance Health 
Damage. Payload is the amount of ammunition a standard magazine or E-Mag would 
contain - Kinetic Magazines are variable in size and are often hand loaded or machine fed, 
while E-Mags are One-Size Fits All manufactured energy packs that fit inside the weapon. 
A WeaponÅfs Rate of Fire is how much of a Payload the Firearm is able to put down range, 
holding down the trigger down longer to take on a larger amount of penalties for the 
benefit of improving the amount of damage the weapon will do for the attack. Weapon 
Range is how many Spaces the weapon may be used within, if the Target is outside of 
Minimum or Maximum Range, a -2 Penalty-to-Hit is applied per excess Space. The 
Weapon Proficiency dictates which WP the Drifter uses to use Weapon Expertises. 
Handiness is the number of Hands required to successfully use the weapon. The WeaponÅfs 
Damage Type indicates what kind of Damage the weapon does, most Default WEapons 
deal either Physical or Energy Damage. Finally any Tags the Weapon has to give it special 
mechanics or features.

Firearms
	The Firearm is the bedrock of the modern military machine, every Drifter has one, every soldier wants a better one, and every 
company wants to build the next best one. Each Default Firearm may be taken as a SD or MD variant with the cost being labeled for 
priority. SD Firearms use conventional ammunition of the old world, 9mm, 5.56, and so on. While deadly if used on the unarmored or 
unaware, they will do little against anyone who is Mega Damage Capable or has any MD Armor. MD Firearms rely on heavy caliber 
rounds or highly charged laser fire with energy weapons - if used on an unsuspecting individual they will be torn apart or disintegrated 
on impact, if they are wearing armor they may survive the initial barrage before itÅfs punctured.

Melee
	Melee Weapons serve as a suitable sidearm for a majority of circumstances, though few soldiers or brave heroes want to be the 
first one face to face with a raging creature or other such monter. A majority of Melee Weapons in the modern day are designed for 
Standard Damage, its value being used to either intimidate or strike a decisive blow in the eye socket of an enemy. MD Melee Weapons 
tend to be either made of MD Capable material such as Dragon Tooth or Palladium, or using specialized technology to augment it, such 
as through Vibrotech.
	Unlike Firearms or other Ranged Weapons, Melee Weapons do not have an established Range, instead they are considered to be 
at Range 0 (or Melee) which indicates that the Target is within the same Space as them or they are in a CQC Situation.

Shields
	While combat operations have gradually escalated to more heavy firepower, when confronting enemies in close quarters or 
escaping the jaws of a monster, shields have seen a resurgence in popular combat. Shields may be used as a Melee Weapon, but their 
Block Capacity allows them to absorb damage from attacks and increase the AR of the Drifter for enhanced protection. When a Shield is 
broken, it will need to be repaired alongside armor and weapons that may have been damaged.

Å@Å@Å@When a Drifter engages in a Wrestling Attack, they are attempting to grapple a Target by gripping them and not letting go. 
Rather than detail the complexities, the Drifter makes a Wrestling Combat Check and if successful, they have established a hold. While 
they have a Hold, they are unable to act except make Wrestling Actions, but the grappled Target may also only take Wrestling Actions. 
The Wrestling Attack has a -4 To Hit for each Size the Target is larger than the Drifter, this is +2 To Hit for Targets that are Smaller than 
the Drifter. 
Å@Å@Å@
Break Out
The Drifter attempts to break the hold they are currently in, they make 
an Opposed Combat Check with a -2 against their aggressor, if they 
succeed, they break the grapple on them. If the Drifter has control of 
the Grapple, they may break it automatically.

Choke
The Drifter attempts to choke out the target, if the target requires 
breath and is able to be choked out, the Drifter begins a countdown of 
the TargetÅfs (HRD / 5). It takes that many Rounds, rounded down, to 
successfully KO the Target.

Pinch
The Drifter deals Punch Damage to the Target, they do not require a 
Combat Check to see if they are successful or not. If the TargetÅfs 
Strength is higher than the DrifterÅfs, then this damage is reduced by two 
steps on the Unarmed Punch Attack Chart.

Reversal
The Drifter attempts to turn the tides of the grapple, placing 
themselves in control of whatÅfs going on, A Drifter is required to beat 
the Grappler with an Opposed Combat Check. 

Slam
The Drifter slams the Target to the ground, dealing Kick Damage, but 
breaking the Hold.

Throw
The Drifter throws the Target as hard as they can away from them, 
they are forcefully moved to an Adjacent Space.

Basic Weapon Workshop
	Should the Drifters find themselves in a rather desperate need for a rather customized weapon, then they may delve deep into 
the backmarkets, exotic traders, lunatic gunsmiths, or the local psychic arms dealer in an attempt to find their perfectly customized tool 
of death. The Weapon Workshop is a quick and dirty way of allowing the GM or the Drifters to customize their weapon to be the 
idealized state of being through modifying its various properties and abilities. While not flawless, nothing beats a Rifle that costs more 
than oneÅfs body and soul to tear apart a wizard at 5 miles away.

Missiles
	Rocket propelled explosive payloads require the use of a Missile Launcher or Missile Pod to be successfully employed. Often 
employed in Anti-Vehicle or Anti-Air Capacities, Missiles have proven to be a decisive factor in many engagements, though are 
expensive to purchase making them often a last resort. A Missile loaded into a weapon takes a full Action to complete, after which they 
may fire the Missile with rules dictated based on the type of Missile being fired.
	Due to the delay in firing the Missile, all effects, including Damage, are calculated at the end of the Round. A Drifter may attempt 
to attack a Missile in flight at a -20 to hit its MSR of 8 - upon taking any Mega Damage, it is destroyed instantly. If an Explosive Missile 
does hit, then if the Target is in Light or Heavy Cover, they may make a FIN Save with their Cover Bonus as a modifier. If successful, 
reduce all of the damage to a single Damage Die due to the shock. If there is no cover or they are in a vehicle, then the Missile will 
automatically hit and deal damage.

Flyswatters - Flyswatters is a missile that explodes upon being 
fired into dozens of flechette rounds for unsuspecting enemies. 
Requires a Combat Check to Hit, it will deal 2d4 Damage per 
Swatter Fired.

Fragmentation & High Explosive- Typical Explosive Missiles. 
Targets a Space and will deal damage to everyone inside of that 
Space. If the Target is in Light or Heavy Cover, they may make a 
FIN Save with their Cover Bonus as a modifier. If successful, reduce 
all of the damage

Heavy & Light Guided Missiles  - Using an Onboard System, the 
Drifter guides the dangerous missile towards a Target. They may 
spend additional Actions to improve their chance to hit their 
Target and deal damage similar to a Fragmentation / High 
Explosive Missiles.

Long Flight Missiles  - Using a delayed action accelerate, Long 
Flight Missiles do not record their explosive damage until the end 
of the Turn after the initial firing Round.

Micro Missiles  - A Missile Payload that breaks apart mid flight to 
distribute a number of additional Micro Missiles to saturate a 
target area. With [Spread] the Missile will deal its damage to all 
Targets in all Zones it affects. Due to the saturation effect, Micro 
Missiles have a -4 to Dodge or Save against them. 

Napalm - A catastrophic missile that saturates a number of 
Spaces in burning napalm. All Targets who fail their Save to resist 
it are also set on fire, dealing 1d10 Mega Damage at the end of 
every Round until it is put out.

Screechers - A horrific sound emanates from these missiles as 
they fly through the air, most animals, monsters, and creatures 
with sensitive hearing attempt to run away unless they can make a 
WIL Save.  

Squash Heads - A broad flat headed missile with the goal of 
disrupting the internal chemistry of the occupant. If fired at a 
Vehicle, will deal 1d4 Endurance / Health Damage to all Occupants. 

Starshells  - Deal no damage, but will illuminate a 6-Space Radius 
around them. The Drifter does not need to roll to hit with Starshells. 
If they were to directly shoot at civilians or infantry with Starshells 
however they will deal 1d2 Explosive Damage.

Armor
	With the endless march of weaponry comes the ceaseless advance of ways to not die to it. 
Armor is the first, last, and often only line of defense that a Drifter has in the field. Through 
sophisticated materials and painstaking work, conventional armor on the Errant Earth is able to 
sustain damage from Mega Damage sources, preventing the soft gooey individual underneath those 
layers being turned into a fond memory for others to recollect. 
	Similar to Weapons, Armor variations have exceeded the ability to successfully categorize 
them as every two-bit bandit or shining hero has their own customized armor rig to suit their needs. 
Though instead of modifying barrel length and ammunition being loaded into it - Armor is primarily 
categorized based on its function and ability to protect the user. 
 
	The two most important facets of Armor are its Durability and its Armor Rating.
	Armor Durability measures the amount of damage the Armor can absorb before it breaks to 
reveal the Drifter inside. Upon taking the appropriate damage, the Armor Durability will be reduced 
first - slowly whittling away the Drifter's options before they are turned into paste. 
	Armor Rating is the ability for the Armor to outright mitigate damage by it either bouncing or 
being rendered ineffective. It is not the measure of their ability to "avoid being hit" similar to NSR, but 
instead their ability to avoid taking damage from a hit that would have occured. Drifters relying on AR 
over their NSR are betting on either surviving effects in an area or hoping their armor can absorb the 
hits they will be taking. Armor Rating is not added together, instead the ÅgBestÅh Armor Rating is taken, 
and any modifiers through different sources of Armor Rating will add to that value.
	The Drifter will have a Maneuverability Modifier. The Maneuverability Modifier is a simple way 
to ascertain how flexible and able to move the Drifter is, taking a penalty to any action that would 
demand fine movement, quick reflexes, or other such ÅgManeuverability Situations.Åh Finally, there is 
Simmer Rating (SR) - Simmer is how hard it is for the Heat Sinks inside the suit of armor to dissipate a 
build up of Magical or Psychic Heat. Without more open ended and breathy armor, Magicians and 
Psychics risk overheating themselves to sometimes explosive results. The SR directly reduces the 
Magician or PsychicÅfs total Heat they are able to draw upon. 
Å@Å@Å@?
Armor Layers
	Traditional Armor Rig Systems are designed in consideration with the three Layers: Under, 
Over, and Plating.
	Under Armour (UA) fights tight to the skin and isn't immediately noticeable to many if they are 
wearing clothing or any other kind of armor. While it doesn't provide exceptional Armor Durability, it 
does provide simple protection at a discounted price.
	Over Armor (OA) is the "default" consideration for most armor types. The Drifter's Over Armor 
is often bulky and built to last, relying on interlocking series of plates or absorbing tissue to mitigate 
damage coming toward them. It is obvious to almost anyone that a Drifter is wearing their Overarmor.
	Finally Plating (PLATE) is accessorized additions fitted to high impact areas and other serious 
considerations. While bulky and extremely obvious, Plating does allow that extra bit of Durability and 
Armor Rating to pull through in desperate circumstances.
	When a Drifter is adorning themselves in their Armor, they may choose to wear one set of 
Under Armour, Over Armor, and Plating of their choice - adding together all of their Armor Durability 
and Armor Rating together to determine their final amount.

Armor Weights
	To measure the protectiveness of each type of Armor, each one will be assigned a different 
Weight Class. The total Weight of the Armor isn't necessarily how heavy it is to hold or lug around, but 
instead the density and reinforced plates that make up the actual armored sections. In short, the 
Weight Class directly correlates the defensive properties of the Armor being worn.
	There are four Weight Classes: Light, Medium, Heavy, and Juggernaut. Each one comes with its 
own bonuses and drawbacks tied to if it is being used as UA, OA, or PLATEs. Mixing and matching 
Weight Classes is possible (Light Under Armor, Heavy Over Armor, Juggernaut Plating).

HEV, PEV, & OEV Variant Suits
Å@Å@Å@Among armorers in the new world, protection from a bullet is the most important aspect of 
armor and associated accessories. Among survivors of the new world, protection from a bullet is often 
the least of their worries as their skin is melting off from radiation. Most UA and OA are built with the 
assumption of being an HEV, PEV, or OEV Suit. Similar to Durability and Armor Rating, Resistances 
between armors do stack, increasing the protection they may possess. However, only the smallest Air 
Supply is considered for purposes of O2 usage. 
Å@Å@Å@Hazardous Environment Suits, or HEV Suits, are top of the line protection against the elements, 
coming with a stabilized environment inside of the armor to allow the wearer to breathe fresh oxygen, 
keep themselves cool in hot environments, and maximize warmth in sub-zero temperatures. A full 
HEV suit offers a computer controlled life support system, with automatic filters for hazardous 
chemicals or gasses, operating with a closed air supply system for five hours, and have inbuilt systems 
for short range (5 Miles) radio communications on a closed network if synced properly. HEV Suits offer 
resistance against various Exposure hazards that the Drifter may face, allowing them the extra 
satisfaction of not dying before the fighting begins. 
Å@Å@Å@HEV Suits have closed helmets to both protect the wearer from physical harm as well as from 
various sources of Exposure - this can be intimidating to some.

Gear & Services
	When it comes to the markets of the new world, itÅfs inevitable that the multitude of gear, 
supplies, and miscellaneous ÅgStuffÅh that the Drifters pick up over time. During their adventures, the 
Drifter will be able to hit the town and spend their Credits on different kinds of gear and supplies that 
they may need for the journey ahead. Rather than have a comprehensive list of ÅgthingsÅh Errant Earth 
has vague categories of supplies that are split up between its Tech Level and overall function.
	As long as the Drifter has a backpack or other pack on their person, they may have eight Pack 
Items on their person at any time in addition to any of their additional gear. Smaller items may be 
classified as Belt size, meaning they can be fitted around the belt of the Drifter to more easily reach. 
They can support three Belt Items at any point.

The Wayward Notes - A Simple Way to Avoid Little Quibbles
	This is a bit stranger than most item lists, so IÅfll be explaining it the best I can. Instead of 
worrying about every individual item, a Drifter asks if he can find an ÅgEntrenching ToolÅh and hits the 
market. If heÅfs in a Civilized Area, heÅfs working at a Industrial Tech Level - GM agrees and sets the 
price of the Travel Gear to about 120 Credits. 
	This Entrenching Tool is a simple metallic object at the end of the day, price being more for 
value and make. A Medieval Entrenching Tool is simpler to make, more rigid and less flexible than 
an Industrial one. Pre-Collapse Entrenching Tools could fold up to a full shovel or be folded into 
each other to fit in the palm of a hand. An Exo Entrenching Tool can be anything from a 
biomechanical thing that digs through anything bar metal or some kind of off kilter device that 
most agree ÅgDigsÅh but may not be the actual use.
	Do not quibble about details - you have an item, you donÅft have an item.

went to ruin and the Tears opened up, the large scale vehicle manufacturers were some of the few 
industries that kept struggling - soon replaced by mavericks and garages creating their ideal 
protection against the elements. When describing a Vehicle, itÅfs important to know that Cars, Trucks, 
Aircraft, and even bipedal Vertical Armored Units fall into the same category. Knowing how to engage 
and deal with these threats may keep a Drifter alive longer than most.

Compact, Mid-Size, Large, Rig, and Titanic. Each of these will be assigned a Vehicle Supertype,

Important Notes on Vehicles
	Vehicles on the Errant Earth are often personalized to the Pilot itself, making it difficult to drive 
another person's ride. To represent this, the Drifter will need to make a Pilot Skill Check to either 
intuitively understand it or spend the next minute attempting to figure out how to operate the vehicle 
(-4 to all Actions and -1 Combat Action).
	A Vehicle can be disabled if its Durability reaches 0, representing major damage to stop it 
functioning. It may be forced to keep going, but will have a -4 / -20% to all Actions and -1 Combat 
Action until it's repaired. If its Hull reaches 0, the Vehicle is destroyed and explodes.
	And scarcely talked about, but important note none the less, Vehicles are expensive and 
people rarely wish to part with them except under duress or by taking the keys from their corpse. 
Calculating the cost here is the ÅgAt MarketÅh Cost - expect purchasing a large vehicle to be much more 
difficult and expensive on the Errant Earth. 
?
Enemies of the Errant Earth
	The Drifters will inevitably come into conflict with others, and the field of battle is indiscriminate 
in its rage and fury. Creating an opposing force is not complicated, but depending on the relative 
"Importance" of the enemy, the creation is different.

Extras
Å@Å@Å@Extras are Characters that are present and assisting / hindering the efforts of the Drifters, but 
do not have a name or a unique relationship to the Drifters themselves. Weather than giving them a 
full set of Skills, Attributes, and Abilities, they instead have a series of Concepts which define who they 
are.
Å@Å@Å@Each Extra has one to three Concepts which define their abilities, broad terms that encompass 
many different skills and abilities in a single phrase or idea. These are ranked from 1 (Terrible) to 18 
(Paragon), reflecting how important the Concept is to the Extra as well as their ability to manipulate it. 
If the Extra needs to make an Attribute Check or Save, they will use the most relevant Concept they 
possess. Thus Backwoods Ranger 10 would have an Attribute score of 10 for everything relevant to 
that Concept. If an Extra needs to perform a Skill Check, they will take their Concept and multiply it by 
5, reflecting their innate abilities in that category. Using the Backwoods Ranger above, they would 
have a 50% to succeed at any Skill Check that would require the use of that Concept.
Å@Å@Å@If an Extra does not have a Concept that is relevant, they will have to Default to their Base 
Competency. Base Competency is taking one of their Concepts and applying a -5 modifier to it. They 
may use the best Concept if it is vaguely relevant to the Extra, if it is completely outside of the realm of 
the Extra, they apply it to their lowest Concept.
Å@Å@Å@From there the Extra is assigned Combat Training, Weapons, Armor, and anything else relevant 
for their role. 

Example
Renegade Scientist
Coalition Pilot
Exo Miner
Mercenary Charlatan
Scientist 12  
Smuggler 7
Pilot 11 
Coalition Soldier 10
Exo 8
Mining 12
Smooth Talker 15
Gunslinger 8

Å@Å@Å@Whenever an Extra is under threat their Health is equal to their largest Concept. Should they 
lose all of their Health, they will either die instantly or be incapacitated. If the Extra is considered an 
MD Creature, they will instead multiply their highest Concept by 3, 5, 7, or 10 to determine how much 
MD they possess. The value is based on the relative danger, size, and effectiveness of the Extra. 
Extras may have benefits based on an Exo Type, Robot Chassis, or other benefits that come from 
these types of backgrounds, but will not benefit from any other aspects. 
?
Advanced Characters
	Advanced Characters are important aspects of Errant Earth that play a part in the story and 
the DrifterÅfs personal struggles. Advanced Characters have Attributes and Skills similar to the Drifters, 
but have a ÅgCurated ListÅh that signify major notes or unique skills they may possess. In addition to 
possessing three to five Concepts, they are able to have a set of Skills that signify their abilities or 
nature. 
	Advanced Characters also adopt one to two Backgrounds or Occupations to signify their 
abilities, their total CL being equal to their highest Concept, minus five, to represent their skills. Any 
benefits gained from these Backgrounds and Occupations may be applied as well, but certain 
restrictions may apply or depend on the Advanced Character is made.

Complete Characters
	Complete Characters are made similarly to the Drifters, selecting Backgrounds and 
Occupations, possessing Attributes, and enjoying the benefits and problems that come from it. 
However, Complete Characters gain additional Karma if they are part of an Opposing Force equal to 
[Number of Drifters x 2] that is added onto their total Karma to purchase additional skills and abilities.
	If the GM wishes, they may assign a set of Concepts to a Complete Character as well, further 
developing their abilities with a broad set of skills in addition to the specifics. Their Attributes and Skills 
would still take priority in this case. 
?
Advancement
	Throughout their adventures across the Errant Earth, the Drifters will be improving themselves 
and their abilities with their trials of fire. When taking into account the life expectancy of the Drifters 
and the lofty goals that they often try to achieve, itÅfs no secret that ÅgHigh LevelÅh Drifters are rare and 
often some of the best around. As the Drifter increases their Character Level, they are also increasing 
the fame that comes with the territory - soon people begin recognizing their work, signature abilities, 
and seeking their assistance with greater and grander projects and adventures.
Å@Å@Å@There are three ways for a Drifter to increase their Character Level, which in turn will increase 
the Rank of all of their currently acquired Backgrounds and Occupations.

Milestones
Å@Å@Å@Under the Milestone System, the Drifters will need to accomplish goals and succeed at plans to 
progress and improve themselves. This method works best with a narrative throughline, such as the 
Drifters being contractors, working for a mercenary company, or focused around a particular set of 
story beats that the GM has set forward. Every time these milestones are reached, the Drifter will 
increase their CL and rise in power. These distinct moments are high stress and dangerous, whether 
resolving a family crisis, undergoing emotional revelations, or simply completing a job to a (relatively) 
satisfactory conclusion.
Å@Å@Å@If the GM allows it, individual Drifters may hit Independent Milestones that pertain to their 
individual storyline or personal hang-ups, the GM is encouraged to never allow a Drifter to deviate 
more than one or two CL from others to maintain the balance and not overshadow the 
accomplishments of the entire team (whoever is taking credit for their deeds is an entirely different 
matter). 	

The Wayward Notes - Replacing the Dead
	ItÅfs tragic, itÅfs terrible, and it may be inevitable. When a Drifter 
dies they will be replaced by another Drifter soon after, joining up 
with the crew out of their own needs or ideals. As the Drifters grow in 
power, the fewer people are actually able to fill the shoes of their 
more competent allies. To represent this, consult the Chart.
	No matter what, after CL 13 all Drifters will end up being CL 12. 
Being Heroes of Humanity are large shoes to fit, and few rise up to 
the challenge.

Numerical System
	The Numerical System requires each Drifter to acquire Experience Points (EXP) from their 
accomplishments and abilities. Each CL requires [1,000 x Level] Experience to reach. These points do 
not roll over from Level to Level, therefore reaching Level 2 is 2,000 EXP, Level 3 is 3,000 EXP. So from 
Level 1 to 3, the total would be a total of 5,000 EXP (2,000 + 3,000).

	Being Part of the Episode and its consequences will always reward the Drifter, those who miss 
Episodes or are unable to attend may make up the EXP elsewhere or through their own 
accomplishments. Simplistic and Complex Objectives are based on the objectives and goals that each 
of these require. ÅgDestroying a TargetÅh is fairly simple, while ÅgDestroying a Target Facility While Saving 
the HostagesÅh is a bit more Complex.	
	Combat Operations indicate that the Drifters experienced a genuine threat, with more EXP 
being awarded for more difficult encounters with dangerous enemies. Competent Plans indicate that 
the Drifters thought out ideas or plans that required foresight and concentration with their Skills and 
history at the forefront (even if those plans fail or are unable to be completed). Finally, Highlighting the 
Weird & Wonderful aspects of the Errant Earth means that the Drifter is using their strange powers, 
skills, or abilities in addition to engaging with the bizarre and mystical in their own unique way. 
	The Numerical System is slower and rewards active participation in the activities going on, 
playing it ÅgSafeÅh will often result in less but more reliable EXP, while being more proactive and 
dangerous will reward more. ItÅfs the DrifterÅfs choice to engage in that kind of chicanery. Additional EXP 
may be rewarded by the GM upon accomplishing objectives in unique ways, succeeding at personal 
objectives and desires, or simply pawning off their treasures and blowing their Credits on a night on 
the town. Experience Points are just as much a measure of experience as well as the willingness to 
experience. 

Deeds
	A hybridized system of the two - Deeds are direct actions that leave a lasting impact on the 
world and the Drifters themselves. Accomplishing missions, tying up loose ends, or reaching homebase 
after a harrowing journey all contribute toward Deeds. Every CL requires a number of Deeds to be 
accomplished equal to the potential CL - thus CL 4 would require four additional Deeds that reset 
upon levelling. Thus CL 1 to CL 4 would require nine Deeds (2 + 3 + 4). The difficulty and scale of the 
Deeds increase as the Drifter builds their fame and fortune, at CL 1 a Deed may be simply surviving a 
journey, while at CL 8 it may demand that the Drifter reaches a farthest point on the map, plunder its 
goods, and make it out alive. 
	Independent Deeds are possible, often requiring the Drifter to undergo their own personal arc 
or perform their own (mis)deeds over their peers. 
Karma Benefits
	Upon reaching a new CL, the Drifter will acquire a set of Karma equal to their current amount of 
Karma of their Backgrounds and Occupations. Similar to when they were first being created, Karma 
may be spent to improve the Drifter in addition to their natural development. Karma may be held onto 
between Character Levels, allowing low Karma Drifters to acquire more expensive benefits and perks 
over a longer period of time.
	Should the Drifter ever have ÅgNegative KarmaÅh they will instead be reset to 0 Karma .

Legacy Occupations
Å@Å@Å@The potential for heroism and displaying nearly superhuman skills are simple on the Errant 
Earth, but few are able to rise to the occasion and find themselves taking on a Legacy Occupation. A 
Legacy Occupation have a CL requirement and often strict demands that the Drifter will need to 
succeed at. If they manage to accomplish all of these feats and earn the right - they may transfer into 
a Legacy Occupation as if it were any other kind of Occupation.
Å@Å@Å@Once the Drifter is locked into a Legacy Occupation, they are unable to leave that Occupation - 
they have cemented themselves in the world as what they are, for better or for worse.

Species Creation System
	If the Drifter is an Exo or a Mutant, they will be relying on the Species Creation System to 
determine the new body parts, appendages, and abilities they have. This is primarily determined via 
calculating the Species Rating when creating the Exo in question or developing the MutantÅfs 
properties. The higher the Species Rating is, the harder it is for the Drifter to Transfer out as well as 
reduce the total Karma the Species has.

Backgrounds

Oni (Race)
Devil Horns, Spirit Warriors
	Oni are the result of years and years of inbreeding among the genetic trash of Domains of the 
Feudal Lords. Their various genetic quirks make them invaluable for the Osama who wish to employ 
their Ågspiritual abilitiesÅh to hunt their enemies, serve in their armies, or simply bloody their blades in their 
name. Due to these factors Oni have a unique position in the Domain System, being above the 
common rabble, but never really being able to increase their standing among the noble Kizoku, let 
alone to claim a title of an Osama.
	The DrifterÅfs bloodline sticks with them, an inevitability that seems to be both a blessing and a 
curse. The Oni who wander are the ones who either seek to make a name for themselves or seek to 
spite that title they have.

Occupations

Samurai (Man-At-Arms)
Loyalist, Bushi, Swordslaves
	When the Domains were first established, the petty warlords who would later become the 
Osama adopted their personal retinue of warriors to make up their armies. These warriors and their 
successors would later become the first of the New Samurai, taking up the mantle of the old worldÅfs 
culture. Samurai are bound to a Domain and the ruling Osama, though loyalties between the two may 
vary drastically between each Samurai. Samurai exist among the Kizoku, but also the Heishi class of 
soldiers, often depending drastically upon their upbringing and personal wealth. 
	Samurai Drifters are those who are on their quest, whether itÅfs for enlightenment, exile, or on a 
prolonged operation of their Domain. They are loyal first to their Domain and the road a far second, 
but their martial excellency and nobility make them an ideal combination for wayward souls.

Ronin (Man-At-Arms)
Broken Swords, Traitors, Ghost Soldiers
	As long as swords have been bound by oath and title, there have been ones attempting to cut 
free from them. Ronin are, or were, Samurai of the Domains - trained in battle halls and making war in 
the name of their Osama. But something changed, it may have been something large, something 
small, or perhaps even a mistake that they had no part in. Whatever that change was they 
abandoned the Samurai Path, instead becoming a ghost of themselves. Whether they treat their new 
found freedom as a blessing, or a curse as they are now hunted by their former brothers-in-arms, is 
up to them.
	Ronin Drifters? All Ronin are adrift in the sea of their own thoughts and troubled loyalties, 
wandering from place to place to ply their deadly trade is a necessity. Drifters following the way of 
the ghost soldier is a Drifter who cut themselves off from a life they once had. A life that seems so long 
ago.

Robot Stuff List


Robotica Cyberntica
	If the Drifter is a Robot or indulging in cybernetics, they will need to consult the Robotics 
Creation System to determine their new make, creation, and additional effects that come from being 
synthetic. Similar to Species Rating, the Robot will need to determine their Robotics Chassis Rating to 
determine how much is packed into their system. The more they have, the more difficult it is for them 
to Transfer out of their steel exterior and actually develop themselves successfully.

Å@Å@Å@Each Robotic Frame	has a number of Slots designed to fit in various features. For example, a 
Humanoid Robot has 3 Sensor Slots to fit in different Sensor Traits, but only 1 CPU Slot. If the Drifter 
desperately needs or wants a Trait that they have no more Slots for, they may sacrifice two from 
other categories to take it. Open Slots may be used for any type of Trait.

Å@Å@Å@Robotic Programming signifies the base expectations and needs of the RobotÅfs purpose. While 
many Robots still follow the Laws of Robotics out of obligation, many others have deviated so far from 
their base programming itÅfs difficult to fully understand them, but their make and model still defines 
their abilities.
Å@Å@Å@Anthropocentric Designs are flairs or minor abilities that assist the Robot in completing their 
task, such as being a portable drink dispenser in addition to other creative flairs to their design, 
exaggerated features, multiple voices, etc.
Å@Å@Å@Features are the Skill Choices that the Drifter has access to and which ones they are able to 
invest in successfully. For example a Industrial Robot may select any number of Technical or Electronic 
& Mechanical Skills to begin with, but cannot take any People Skills.

Cybertroniks
	Drifters who lose limbs willingly or not will most likely begin indulging in Cybernetics to 
compensate for the lack of other aspects. They will first need to calculate to see how much their body 
can sustain through the use of their Cybernetic Stress. 

Cybernetic Stress Calculation
[HRD]
If Cybernetic Stress Exceeds Limit, reduce HP to compensate.

	Basic Cybernetics allow the Drifter to augment various aspects of their body by replacing limbs 
or other essential components with technology. Base Cybernetics (Cyber Arm, Cyber Legs, etc) are 
entirely defined by their Modifier which the Drifter will need to determine and purchase when they 
find what they like. For example, a Cybertronik Arm that is Standard Grade granting a +2 to POW 
would be 2000 Credits with the amount of Cybernetic Stress is takes being (2 * 1d10). Every installation 
runs the risk of exceeding their Cybernetic Stress as their body begins to fail rapidly on the operating 
table.

Å@Å@Å@Drifters who want to push their bodies to the limit may also opt to install more advanced 
cyberware, often being derivatives of Robotic Chassis Parts. They will multiple the Robot Chassis Cost 
by 500 for the basic installation fee, not the acquisition of the parts - that would be [Robotic Chassis 
Cost * 1000] minimum. The Human Deviation is how much Cybernetic Stress results from it, replacing 
the Modifier in the equations above and adding +5.
Å@Å@Å@The Drifter also has Slots similar to their Robotic compatriots, able to take a number of 
Cybernetics in their body. However if the Drifter installs INVASIVE Cybernetics, then it counts for the 
main Slot and one other of choice. Uninstalling Cybernetics costs the same as the installation fee and 
removes half of the Cybernetic Stress caused by the part. Invasive Cybernetics cannot be Uninstalled 
(bar the more permanent uninstalling methods).
